fut. ἱμάσω [α] ; aor. ἵμασα ; (< ἱμάς) : — flog horses, τοὺς ἵμασ’ Ἀντίλοχος Il. 5.589, cf. 11.531 ; of men, εἰ… σε πληγῇσιν ἱμάσσω 15.17, cf. Hes. Th. 857 ; ἵμασε χθόνα χειρί smote it, h.Ap. 340 ; ὅτε… γαῖαν ἱμάσσῃ when he smites it with lightnings, Il. 2.782 ; — Pass., ἱμασσόμενος δέμας αὔραις AP 7.696 (Arch.), cf. Nonn. D. 42.491.
to be a clothier, IGRom. 4.1209 (Thyatira) (nisi leg. πραγματ-).
όν, loaded with apparel, ναῦς Thphr. Lap. 68.
τό, Dim. of ἱμάτιον, Ar. Fr. 90.
τό, Dim. of ἱμάτιον, Ar. Pl. 985, Lys. Fr. 316S., BGU 1103.12 (i BC) ; by crasis with the Art., θαἰματίδια Ar. Lys. 401.
fut. -ιῶ, furnish with clothing, UPZ 2.14 (ii BC), etc. ; — Pass., τοῦ παιδὸς τρεφομένου καὶ ἱματιζομένου POxy. 275.14 (i AD) ; γυνὴ ἱματισμένη ἔχιδνα Secund. Sent. 8 ; ἱματισμένος Ev. Marc. 5.15.
ἡ, wardrobe, IG2². 1672.229, 309, Hsch. s.v. κανδυτάναι.
ὁ, clothes-seller, Luc. Merc. Cond. 38, Pseudol. 21.
ου, ὁ clothes-stealer, DL. 6.52.
ου, ὁ one who lets out actor΄s costumes, IG 12(9).207.22 (Eretria, iii BC), SIG 424.85 (Delph., iii BC), Poll. 7.78, AB 100.
οῦ, ὁ, = ἱματιομίσθης, Poll. 7.78.

τό, in form a Dim. of ἷμα (i.e. εἷμα), a piece of dress ; in usage always of an outer garment, formed by an oblong piece of cloth worn above the χιτών, Ar. Ec. 333, IG2². 1524.205, al., D. 24.114, etc. ; λαμπρὸν ἱ. ἔχων Epich. [277] ; θοἰμάτιον by crasis for τὸ ἱμ-, Ar. Nu. 179, al. ; θοἰμάτιον καθεὶς ἄχρι τῶν σφυρῶν D. 19.314 ; ἱματίων ἕλξεις Pl. Alc. 1.122c ; of the Roman toga, Plu. Brut. 17, Cor. 14 ; hence ἐν ἱματίοις, of civilians, = togati, Id. Cam. 10 ; but ἱ. Ἑλληνικόν, opp. the toga, Luc. Merc. Cond. 25. ἱμάτια, τά, generally, clothes, Hdt. 1.9, Pl. Plt. 279e, D. 27.10 ; by crasis, θαἰμάτια Hippon. 83.1, Ar. V. 408 (lyr.), Lys. 1093 ; of grave-clothes, ἐν εἱμ. τρισὶ [θάπτειν] IG 12(5).593.2 (Iulis, v/iv B.), cf. Plu. Sol. 21. metaph, ἱμάτια πόλεως τείχη Eust. 1871.50. generally, cloth, Hdt. 4.23, DS. 14.109, Ael. VH 8.7, Iamb. VP 21.100. [ἱμ- in Att. Inscrr., IG1². 427, 386.18, 2².1514.16, etc. ; εἱμ- ib. 12(5) l.c. (εμ- lap.), 5(1).1390.16, al. (Andania, i BC), which is easier to explain, v. εἷμα, εἱματισμός.]
ου, ὁ, collector of deliveries in kind in the form of clothing, BGU 1564.1 (ii AD).
ου, ὁ, = κναφεύς, dub. in ib. 118iii7 (ii AD).
ἡ, clothes-making, Gloss.
ου, ὁ, = ἱματιοπώλης, Stud.Pal. 22.95.2 (iii AD).

ου, ὁ, clothes-dealer, Critias Fr. 64D., UPZ 8.32 (ii BC), AJP 38.418 (Egypt), Ephes. 3 p. 146 (εἱμ-), Ptol. Tetr. 179 ; — also in form εἱματοπώλης, Gloss. ; — fem. ἱματιόπωλις, ιδος, IG 2.3650, Ath. 3.76a ; ἡ ἱ. ἀγορά Poll. 7.78.
(sc. τέλος), τό, tax on clothes-dealers, PLeipz. 5.7 (Ber. Sächs. Ges. d. W. 37.245 (iii AD)).
ή, όν, skilled in making clothes ; ἡ ἱματιουργική (sc. τέχνη) the tailor΄s art, Pl. Plt. 280a, Gal. Thras. 26.
τό, = ἱματιοφορίς, Sammelb. 7033.42, 43 (v AD).
ίδος, ἡ, portmanteau, POxy. 116.10 (ii AD), Ammon. Diff. p. 135 V. (cf. Ptol.Ascal. p. 406H.), Ael. Dion. Fr. 206.
take care of clothes, Luc. Hipp. 8.
τό, wardrobe, Gloss. ; — also in form εἱματοφυλάκιον, ib.
ακος, ὁ, ἡ, keeper of the wardrobe, LXX 4Ki. 22.14 ; — in form εἱματοφύλαξ, Gloss.

ὁ, clothing, apparel, Thphr. Char. 23.8, Aen.Tact. 31.15, SIG 1015.35 (Halic., iii BC), PHib. 1.54 (iii BC), PCair. Zen. 28.1 (iii BC), BCH 6.24 (Delos, ii BC), Plb. 11.9.2, Ev. Luc. 7.25, Plu. Alex. 39 ; εἱμ- PEleph. 1.4 (iv BC), IG 5(1).1390.15 (Andania, i BC), etc.

Att. inf. ἱμῆν Phot. : — draw up, esp. water from a well, Ath. 8.352a ; κάδῳ Orib. Eup. 1.1.2 ; — Pass., to be tapped of, yield, γάλα Arist. HA 522b12, PA 688b10. (From ἱμάς 2f, acc. to Ael. Dion. Fr. 211 ; ἱμάω has ι (v. καθιμάω), like ἱμονιά, ἱμανήθρη, but ἱμαῖος has ι.)
= ἔγχελυς, at Methymna, Hsch. (cf. Lith. ungurỹs ΄eel΄).
ἡ, the island of Imbros, Il. 13.33, etc. ; also, epith. of Pelasgian Hermes, St.Byz. s.v. ; hence Ἴμβριοι, οἱ, the Imbrians, IG1². 198.101.

Aeol. ἰμέρρω Sappho 1.27, Alc. Supp. 26.5, cf. Hdn. Gr. 2.949 ; (< ἵμερος) : — long for, desire, c. gen., τί κακῶν ἱμείρετε τούτων… ; Od. 10.431, cf. 555, Hes. Sc. 31 ; μεγάλων B. 1.62 ; μάχης A. Ag. 940 ; βίου S. Fr. 952, cf. Ar. Nu. 435 ; c. inf., long or wish to do, Alc. l.c., Sol. 13.7, A. Pers. 233, S. OT 587, Ichn. 128 ; ὄσσα μοι τέλεσσαι θῦμος ἰμέρρει Sappho l.c. ; c. Adj. neut., γνωτὰ κοὐκ ἄγνωτά μοι προσήλθεθ’ ἱμείροντες S. OT 59 ; abs., Id. El. 1053 ; ἀσμένοις… καὶ ἱμείρουσιν… τὸ φῶς ἐγίγνετο Pl. Cra. 418d.
Med. ἱμείρομαι, aor.1 ἱμειράμην Il. 14.163 ; — Pass., aor.1 ἱμέρθην Hdt. 7.44 ; c. gen., ὁππότ’ ἂν ἡβήσῃ τε καὶ ἧς ἱμείρεται αἴης (Ep. aor. subj.) Od. 1.41 ; χρημάτων ἱ. μεγάλως Hdt. 3.123 ; c. inf., εἴ πως ἱμείραιτο παραδραθέειν φιλότητι (cf. ἵμερος) Il. 14.163, cf. Od. 1.59, Hdt. 6.120, S. OT 386. — Ep., Ion. (Hdt. and Hp. Morb. 4.39), and Trag. word ; never in Att. Prose ; introduced as etym. in Pl. Cra. l.c.
ἴμεναι [ι], Ep. inf. of εἶμι (ibo).
ἡ, old collat. form of ἡμέρα, acc. to Pl. Cra. 418c, 418d.
υκος, ἡ, with lovely diadem, θεά B. 16.9.
ον, with lovely limbs, B. 12.137.

εσσα, εν, (< ἵμερος) exciting desire, lovely, charming, in Hom. always of things, ἱμερόεντα… ἔργα γάμοιο Il. 5.429, etc. ; χροὸς ἱμερόεντος 14.170 ; ἀοιδή, ἔπεα, Od. 1.421, 17.519 ; γόος (cf. ἵμερος) 10.398 ; Χαρίτων χορὸν ἱμερόεντα 18.194, cf. Il. 18.603 ; ἱμερόεν κιθάριζε ib. 570 ; so later κισσός DP. 947 ; ἔρωτες AP 5.277 (Agath.) ; of persons, Pi. Fr. 87 (Sup.), Thgn. 1365 (Sup.), Theoc. 7.118 ; νύμφη Coluth. 295.
ές, (< θάλλω) Dor. for ἱμεροθηλής, sweetly blooming, ἔαρ AP 9.564 (Nicias) ; vulg. ἡμεροθαλής.
ουν, lovely of soul, Orph. H. 56.8.
Pass., of a female, have sexual intercourse with, τοῦ ἀνδρός, or abs., Hp. Mul. 1.12, 24.
πνουν, breathing sweetness, BMus.Inscr. 1084.

ὁ, longing, yearning after, c. gen. rei, σίτου… περὶ φρένας ἵμερος αἱρεῖ Il. 11.89, etc. ; γόου ἵμερον ὦρσε raised [in them] a yearning after tears, i.e. a desire of the soul to disburden itself in grief, 23.14 ; ὑφ’ ἵμερος ὦρτο γόοιο Od. 16.215, etc. ; with gen. obj. added, πατρὸς ὑφ’ ἵμερον ὦρσε γόοιο for his father, 4.113 ; ἵμερον ἔχειν, = ἱμείρεσθαι, c. inf., Hdt. 5.106, 7.43 ; ἵμερος ἔχει με… ἰδεῖν S. OC 1725 (lyr.), cf. Sappho Supp. 24.11 ; ἵ. ἐπείρεσθαί μοι ἐπῆλθέ Hdt. 1.30, cf. 9.3 ; τῶν (sc. δενδρέων) γλυκὺς ἵ. ἔσχεν… φυτεῦσαι Pi. O. 3.33 ; in pl., πολλοὶ γὰρ εἰς ἓν ξυμπίτνουσιν ἵ. various impulses or emotions, A. Ch. 299, cf. Phld. Ir. p. 37 W., Piet. 20. abs., desire, love, ὥς σεο νῦν ἔραμαι καί με γλυκὺς ἵ. αἱρεῖ Il. 3.446 ; δὸς νῦν μοι φιλότητα καὶ ἵ. 14.198 ; δαμέντα φρένας ἱμέρῳ Pi. O. 1.41, cf. Sappho Supp. 25.16 ; ἱμέρῳ πεπληγμένος A. Ag. 544 ; ἱμέρου νικώμενος Id. Supp. 1005, cf. Pr. 649, S. Tr. 476, Ar. Ra. 59 ; βλεφάρων ἵ. S. Ant. 796 (lyr.). personified, Χάριτές τε καὶ Ἵ. Hes. Th. 64 ; Ἔρως… χαρίτων, ἱμέρου, πόθου πατήρ Pl. Smp. 197d, cf. Luc. DDeor. 20.15, Nonn. D. 1.68, al. as Adj., only in neut. as Adv., ἵμερον αὐλήσαντι AP 9.266 (Antip.) ; ἵμερα μελίζεσθαι, δακρῦσαι, ib. 7.30 (Antip.Sid.), 364 (Marc. Arg.). — Poet., exc. in Pl. and Ion. and later Prose, as Hdt. ll.cc., Hp. Aër. 22, Phld. ll.cc., Acad. Ind. p. 56M. (Sts. derived fr. is-mero-, cf. Skt. iṣṭás ΄desired΄, iṣmás ΄god of love΄, but Aeol. texts have ἴμερος, ἰμέρρω, never ἰμμ- ; cf. ἡμερτόν· ἐπέραστον, Hsch. (s.v.l.).)
ονος, ὁ, ἡ, lovely in spirit, Doroth. ap. Heph.Astr. 3.9.
ον, of lovely voice or song, ἀηδών Sappho 39, Alcm. 26 (vulg. ἱεροφ-), Theoc. 28.7.
Aeol. for ἱμείρω.

ή, όν, (< ἱμείρω) longed for, desired, lovely, Τιταρήσιος Il. 2.751 ; ὕδατα ARh. 2.939 ; Σαλαμίς Sol. 1.1 ; κίθαρις h.Merc. 510 ; στέφανοι Hes. Th. 577 ; κόμα Sappho 119 ; λέχος Pi. P. 3.99 ; ἀοιδαί, δόξα, Id. O. 6.7, P. 9.75 ; ἱ. ἡλικίη dear life, Simon. 115 ; of persons, AP 5.297 (Jul.) ; epith. of Apollo and Dionysus, ib. 9.524.10, 525.10. — Poet. and later Prose, as Epicur. Fr. 165, Luc. DDeor. 20.15 ; ἱμερτόν, τό, Plu. 2.926f ; ἐφ’ ἱμερτοῖσιν prob. from a poet, ib. 394b.
ες, = ἱμερόεις, Callistr. Stat. 11.
Prep., c. gen., between, ἰ. Πελειᾶν Schwyzer 664.17 (Orchom. Arc., iv BC) ; also ἰμέσουν τοῖς Διδύμοιυν ib. 25 ; prob. fr. ἰν(= ἐν)μεσ-.
δίκη (Sicel), Hsch.
ή, όν, (< ἱμάω) drawn out as from a well, Hsch.
ὑπόζωσον (-στον cod.) (Cypr.), Hsch.
(ἰνμενφής lap.), v. ἐμμεμφής.
poet. for ἴμεναι, ἰέναι, inf. of εἶμι (ibo).

[prob. ῑ, cf. An.Ox. 1.217], ἡ, (< ἱμάς) well-rope, Alex. 174.9, Apollod. Gel. 1 (pl.), Ph. 2.89 (pl.), Luc. Icar. 7, JConf. 8, Hsch. ; ἱμονιάν (abs.) a rope΄s length, i.e. as long as a bucket takes to go down and come up a well, Ar. Ec. 351.
ὁ, water-drawer, Ar. Ra. 1297.
πόλεμοι, Hsch.
v. ἔμπασις.
ἔμβλεψον (Paph.), Hsch.
ἡ, Arc. for ἐμπλατία, a sacrificial cake, IG 5(2).4 (Tegea, iv BC).
v. ἐμπολή.
ληπτής, Hsch. (perh. Arc. for ἐμπολεύς).
v. ἴπτω.
Arc. for ἐμφορβίω (Tegea, iv BC).
epith. of Poseidon in Syria, Hsch.
in compds., = ἰν–, Arc., Cypr., Cret. for ἐν–.
Arc., Cypr., and Cret. for ἐν.
dat. and acc. of the old pers. Pron. ἵ.
or εἵν, gen. εἱνός, τό, an Egyptian and Jewish liquid measure, LXX Ex. 29.40, al., J. AJ 3.9.4, Eust. 1282.51 (indecl. in LXX ll.cc.) ; cf. ἵνιον.

A. Adv., I. of Place,
1. in that place, there, once in Hom., ἵ. γάρ σφιν ἐπέφραδον ἠγερέθεσθαι Il. 10.127 (acc. to Eust.).
2. elsewh. relat., in which place, where, 2.558, Od. 9.136, Hdt. 2.133, 9.27, 54, Pi. O. 1.95, B. 10.79, A. Pr. 21, al., S. El. 22, 855, Ar. Ra. 1231, etc. ; rarely in Att. Prose, Lys. 13.72 (v. infr.), Pl. Ap. 17c, Phlb. 61b ; ἵ. ἡ Νίκη (sc. ἐστίν) IG2². 1407.13 ; rare in later Greek, Arr. An. 1.3.2, Luc. Cont. 22, Ind. 3 ; with particles, ἵ. τε Il. 20.478 ; ἵ. περ 24.382, Od. 13.364, Lys. l.c. ; ἵν’ ἄν c. subj., wherever, S. OC 405, E. Ion 315 ; as indirect interrog., Hdt. 1.179, 2.150, E. Hec. 1008.
b. after Hom., like other Advs. of Place, c. gen., ἵ. τῆς χώρης Hdt. 1.98 ; ἔμαθε ἵ. ἦν κακοῦ in what a calamity, Id. 1.213 ; οὐδ’ ὁρᾶν ἵν’ ἐ̓ κακοῦ S. OT 367 ; ἵν’ ἕσταμεν χρείας ib. 1442 ; ἵν’ ἦμεν ἄτης Id. El. 936 ; ὁρᾷς ἵν’ ἐσμὲν αὐτοῦ πέρι τῆς ἀπορίας Pl. Sph. 243b.
c. with Verbs of motion, whither, Od. 4.821, al. ; ὁρᾷς ἵν’ ἥκεις S. OT 687, al., Din. 2.10 ; ἵναπερ ὥρμητο Th. 4.74.
ΙI. of circumstance, γάμος…, ἵ. χρή at which, when, Od. 6.27 ; ἵ. μὲν ἐξῆν αὐτοῖς…, ἐνταῦθα.
when it was in their power, Antipho 6.9.
2. = ἐάν, dub. in Il. 7.353 (v.l. ἵν’ ἄν, cf. Sch.), Archil. 74.7 codd., v.l. in Din. 1.1, and Pl. Chrm. 176b.
B. Final Conj., that, in order that, from Hom. downwards, mostly first word in the clause, but sts. preceded by an emphatic word, Pl. Chrm. 169d ; ἵ. δή Il. 7.26, 23.207, Hdt. 1.29, Pl. R. 420e, 610c ; never with ἄν or κε (if found, these particles belong to the Verb, as in Od. 12.156, E. IA 1579).
I. general usage ; with subj., after primary tenses of ind., also subj. and imper. ; pres. ind., Il. 3.252, Od. 2.111, X. Mem. 3.2.3, Cyr. 1.2.11, Isoc. 3.2 ; pf. ind., Il. 1.203, Isoc. 4.129 ; fut., Od. 2.307, 4.591, X. Cyr. 1.2.15 ; subj., S. OT 364 ; imper., Il. 19.348, al., A. Pr. 61, S. Ph. 880, Ar. Ra. 297, Pl. R. 341b, Men. 71d. after historical tenses, in similes, where the aor. is gnomic, Od. 5.490 (αὔοι codd.) ; where aor. is treated as equiv. to pf., Il. 9.99, Od. 8.580, Hdt. 5.91, Lys. 1.4, D. 9.26 ; when the purpose is regarded from the point of view of the speaker΄s present, σὲ παῖδα ποιεύμην ἵ. μοι… λοιγὸν ἀμύνῃς Il. 9.495, cf. Hdt. 1.29, 6.100, Th. 1.44, al., Lys. 1.11, 12, al. after opt. and ἄν, when opt. with οὐκ ἄν is used with sense of imper., Il. 24.264, Od. 6.58 ; after βουλοίμην ἄν…, Lys. 7.12. after impf. with ἄν, D. 23.7. with opt., after historical tenses, Il. 5.3, Od. 3.2, A. Th. 215, Lys. 3.11, Pl. Prt. 314c, etc. ; after the historical pres., E. Hec. 11 ; sts. both moods, subj. and opt., follow in consecutive clauses, Od. 3.77, Hdt. 8.76, 9.51, D. 23.93, 49.14. after opt., Od. 18.369, S. Ph. 325 ; βούλοιντ’ ἂν ἡμᾶς ἐξολωλέναι, ἵνα… λάβοιεν Ar. Pax 413. rarely after primary tenses, by a shifting of the point of view, Od. 17.250, Ar. Ra. 24, Pl. R. 410c. with past tenses of ind., after unfulfilled wishes, Id. Cri. 44d. after ind. with ἄν, to express a consequence which has not followed or cannot follow, S. OT 1389, Pl. Men. 89b, D. 29.17 ; esp. after ἐβουλόμην ἄν…, Ar. V. 961, Lys. 4.3. after such Verbs as ἐχρῆν, ἔδει, E. Hipp. 647, Pl. Prt. 335c, Smp. 181e, Euthd. 304e, Isoc. 9.5, D. 24.48, Men. 349.5, etc. ; when an unfulfilled obligation is implied, τεθαύμακα ὅτι οὐκ εἶπεν (= ἔδει εἰπεῖν)… ἵ.… Pl. Tht. 161c ; ἀντὶ τοῦ κοσμεῖν (= δέον κοσμεῖν)… ἵ.… D. 36.47. after pres. ind. in general statements (including the past), οὐδὲ γὰρ τὸ εἶναι ἔχει ἡ ὕλη, ἱ. ἀγαθοῦ ταύτῃ μετεῖχεν Plot. 1.8.5. ἵ. μή as the neg. of ἵνα, that not, Il. 19.348, etc.
ΙI. special usages ; like ὅπως, after Verbs of command and entreaty, is common only in later Gr. (but cf. Od. 3.327 with ib. 19), ἀξιοῦν ἵ.… Decr. ap. D. 18.155 ; δεήσεσθαι ἵ.… DH. 1.83 ; παρακαλεῖν ἵ.… Arr. Epict. 3.23.27 ; freq. in NT, ἐκήρυξαν ἵ. μετανοήσωσιν Ev. Marc. 6.12, al. ; of will, ὅσα ἐὰν θέλητε ἵ. ποιῶσιν. ib. 25 ; hence ἵ. c. subj. stands for infin., ἐν τούτῳ ἵ. καρπὸν φέρητε (= ἐν τῷ φέρειν) Ev. Jo. 15.8, etc. ; πρῶτόν ἐστιν ἵ. κοιμηθῶ Arr. Epict. 1.10.8, cf. M.Ant 8.29 ; also for ὥστε, LXX Ge. 22.14, al., Plu. 2.333a, Porph. Abst. 2.33, etc.
because, ἵ. ἀναγνῶ ἐτιμήθην I was honoured because I read, Anon. ap. ADysc. Synt. 266.5, cf. Conj. 243.21, Choerob. in Theod. 2.257, al. ; not found in literature. elliptical usages, where the purpose of the utterance is stated, Ζεὺς ἔσθ΄, ἵν’ εἰδῇς ΄tis Zeus, — [I tell thee this] that thou may΄st know it, S. Ph. 989 ; ἵ. μὴ εἴπω ὅτι οὐδεμιᾷ Pl. R. 507d ; ἵ. συντέμω D. 45.5 ; ἵν’ ἐκ τούτων ἄρξωμαι Id. 21.43 ; ἵ. δῶμεν. granted that…, S.E. P. 2.34, cf. 1.79. in commands, introducing a principal sentence, ἵ. συντάξῃς order him…, PCair. Zen. 240.12 (iii BC) ; ἵ. λαλήσῃς PSI 4.412.1 (iii BC) ; ἵ. ἐλθὼν ἐπιθῇς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῇ Ev. Marc. 5.23, cf. 2 Ep. Cor. 8.7, LXX 2 Ma. 1.9, Arr. Epict. 4.1.41, Did. ap. Sch. S. OC 156. ἵ. τί (sc. γένηται) ; to what end? either abs. or as a question, Ar. Ec. 719 ; or with a Verb following, Id. Pax 409, cf. Pl. Ap. 26d, etc. ; ἵ. δὴ τί ; Ar. Nu. 1192. in indignant exclamations, to think that… ! Σωκράτης ἵ. πάθῃ ταῦτα Arr. Epict. 1.29.16.
ΙII. in later Gr. with ind., LXX Ex. 1.11, al., Ep. Gal. 2.4, 4.17, etc.
ΙV. w. τοῦ and inf., ἵ. τοῦ τὰ ὅλα συντελεσθῆναι OGI 5.15 (letter of Antigonus Monophthalmus, iv BC).
ἡ, force, strength of a swell or current at sea, Peripl. M.Rubr. 46 (ἰνδία cod.), Hsch.
v. ἐναλίνω.
Cret., = ἔναντι, GDI 5125a1.
τό, Dim. of ἴς, strand, fibre, ἰ. λεπτὸν καὶ μακρόν Phlp. in Mete. 61.31.
fut. -άσω, = ἰνόω, ἰσχὺν παρέχω, Choerob. in Theod. 2.154, EM 100.39, Suid. ; ὅταν μ’ ἰνάσσατο (sic cod.) Call. Fr. anon. 126.

ὁ, Inachus, a river of Argolis, A. Fr. 168, E. El. 1.
ΙΙ. son of Oceanus, king of Argos, A. Pr. 663, al. ; — Adj. Ἰνάχειος, α, ον, ib. 590.
= ἰνέω.
epith. of the Moon, dub.sens. in PMagPar. 1.2273.

almost always used in pres. and impf. ; aor. ἰνδάλθην Lyc. 597, 961, Max. 163 : — appear, seem, ἄλλοι μοι δοκέουσι παροίτεροι ἔμμεναι ἵπποι, ἄλλος δ’ ἡνίοχος ἰνδάλλεται Il. 23.460 ; ἰνδάλλετο δέ σφισι πᾶσι τεύχεσι λαμπόμενος μεγαθύμου Πηλεΐωνος 17.213 (μεγαθύμῳ Πηλεΐωνι Aristarch., cf. 2), cf. Od. 3.246, h.Ven. 178 ; ὥς μοι ἰνδάλλεται ἦτορ as my memory seems to me, or perh., as my heart pictures him, Od. 19.224 ; also in Att., ὥστ’ ἔμοιγ’ ἰνδάλλεται ὁμοιότατος κλητῆρος εἶναι πωλίῳ Ar. V. 188 ; τοῦτο γάρ μοι ἰ. διανοουμένη [ἡ ψυχή], οὐκ ἄλλο τι ἢ διαλέγεσθαι it seems to me to be merely engaged in a dialogue, Pl. Tht. 189e ; τὰ δι’ ὀφθαλμῶν ἰνδαλλόμενα ἡμῖν Arist. Mu. 397b18, cf. Iamb. Myst. 2.3 ; flash on one΄s mind, ἀμφὶ δὲ… μεληδόνες ἰνδάλλοντο appeared, ARh. 3.812, cf. 2.545. c. dat., resemble, θεοὶ ξένοις ἰνδαλλόμενοι Pl. R. 381e, cf. Lg. 959a ; ἀργύρῳ Theoc. 22.39 ; κύκνοις Lyc. 597. (Never in Trag. ; connected with vid-, Εἴδω.)

ατος, τό, form, appearance, LXX Wi. 17.3, Ael. NA 17.35 ; ἴ. ψυχῆς, = εἴδωλον, IG 3.1403 ; pl., ἰ. ζωῆς Plot. 1.4.3 ; κρυφίων ἰνδάλματα πυρσῶν AP 5.250 (Iren.) ; mental image, ἰ. καὶ δόκησις ψυχῆς Them. Or. 26.327d ; in pl., hallucinations, Luc. Gall. 5, Aret. SD 1.6.
= ἰνδάλλομαι, dub. in Lib. Descr. 30.1.
ὁ, = ἴνδαλμα, in pl., Hp. Ep. 18 ; title of work by Timon, DL. 9.65, 105.
τό, name of an eye-salve, Aët. 7.118.
μεσημβρία (Maced.), Hsch.
v. ἐνδικάζω.
(-πλεύστης cod.), dyer, Gloss.
v. ἔνδικος.

ή, όν, Indian ; ἡ Ἰ. χώρη Hdt. 3.98 ; Sup. -ώτατος Philostr. VA 1.10 ; — fem. Ἰνδίς, ίδος, f.l. in Nonn. D. 17.377. Ἰνδικὸν φάρμακον a kind of pepper, Hp. Mul. 1.81 ; but, indigo (cf. infr. 2), PHolm. 11.2 ; also called ἰ. μέλαν ib. 9.8. the plant indigo, Indigofera tinctoria, Dsc. 5.92. name of an eye-salve, Gal. 12.780, al.
Adv. in the Indian language, Ctes. Fr. 57.4.
ές, born in India, Man. 1.297.
ου, ὁ, Indian-killer, of Dionysus, AP 9.524.

ή, όν, Indian, Hdt. 3.38, al., cf. A. Supp. 284 ; esp. of the drivers of elephants, Phylarch. 36 J., Plb. 1.40.15, al. Ἰνδός, ὁ, the river Indus, Hdt. 4.44, etc. name of a fallacy, Plu. 2.133b. as Adj., = Ἰνδικός, Indian, AP 9.544.1 (Addaeus). Ἰνδή, ἡ, (sc. ἔμπλαστρος) name of a plaster, Orib. Fr. 88.
ἡ, the country on the banks of the Indus, Ptol. Geog. 7.1.
ὁ, mole (< ἀσπάλαξ), Hsch.
ὁ, = Ἰνδολέτης Nonn. D. 17.387.
α, ον, = Ἰνδικός, Nonn. D. 17.380, St.Byz.
τό, sanctuary of Ino, Sch. Euph. Oxy. 2085 Fr. 1.15.
τείνει, Hsch.
or ἰνάω, carry off by evacuations, Ion. word, Hsch., Phot. ; fut. Med. ἰνήσομαι Hp. Mul. 1.52, and prob. l. ib. 119 ; in pass. sense, Id. Loc. Hom. 27 ; — Pass., ἰνῶνται, ἰνώμενος, ibid., ib. 33.
ἡ, = ἴς¹, ταῖς ἀπὸ τῶν καλάμων ἴναις Peripl. M.Rubr. 65.
ὁ, emptying, purging, Hp. Loc. Hom. 16, 33.
εως, ἡ, = ἰνηθμός, Hp. Loc. Hom. 20 (νῆσις codd., cf. Erot. s.v. ἰνήσεται), Pherecyd. 66 J.

τό, (< ἴς¹) occipital bone, occiput, [τοῦ τριχωτοῦ κρανίου]… τὸ ὀπίσθιον [ἐστὶν] ἰνίον Arist. HA 491a33, cf. Gal. UP 9.17, al. ; κεφαλῆς κατὰ ἰνίον Il. 5.73 ; διὰ ἰνίου ἦλθεν [δόρυ] 14.495, cf. Hp. Aph. 3.26, Pherecyd. 66 J., Theoc. 25.264, Euph. 41, Plu. Mar. 33. (ἰ- codd., κατ’ ἰν- Gal. l.c., but cf. ἐφινίους· τὰς ἐπὶ τοῦ ἰνίου σάρκας, Hsch.)
τό, Dim. of ἵν, an Egyptian measure of capacity, PSI 4.333.6 (iii BC), Kalbfleisch Ind. Lect. Rost. 1902.10 (ii AD), PLond. ined. 186 (ii AD), Gal. 19.769.

ὁ, son, A. Eu. 323, Supp. 42, prob. in Id. Ag. 717, cf. E. Tr. 571, HF 354, Lyc. 570, Isyll. 53 (dub.), Call. Aet. 3.1.63, IG 12(8). p. vii (Egypt) ; — fem. ἶνις, ἡ, daughter, E. IA 119. — Trag. only in lyr. ; Prose only in Cypr. dialect, Inscr.Cypr. 101, al.
Arc. for ἐνέστιος.
ἐγκατάβλεψον, Hsch.
v. ἐμμεμφής.
κόρην μικράν, καὶ τὴν ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ, Hsch.
ὁ, = γίννος, Hsch.
παῖδας, Hsch.; cf. ἶνις.
(< ἴς) make strong and nervous, Hdn. Epim. 49 ; — Pass., ἰνῶνται (also ἰννοῦνται), glossed by ζῶσιν, Hsch.
Arc. for ἐμπολή, IG 5(2).3.27 (pl., Tegea, iv BC).
τό, v. sub ἴντυβος.
ὁ, (ἴντουβος Edict.Diocl. 6.3) = ἔντυβος, endive, Gal. 6.628 ; — also ἰντυβολάχανον, τό, [Id.] 14.321.
(ἰνν- cod.)· κλαίει, ὀδύρεται, Hsch. ; — also ἰνύεσθαι· κοσμεῖν, ἱδρύνεσθαι, and ἰνύρετο· ἐμύρετο, Id.
= ἴυγξ, Hsch.
v. ἐμφορβίειν.
v. ἐμφορβισμός.
ες, fibrous, of parts of animals, X. Cyn. 4.1, Arist. HA 497a21 ; ἰνωδέστατον αἷμα Id. PA 651a3 ; of vegetables, φλοιός, φύλλον, Thphr. HP 3.12.1, 5, cf. Dsc. 4.20 ; sinewy, X. Cyn. 4.1.
όος contr. οῦς, ἡ, Ino, daughter of Cadmus, worshipped as a sea-goddess by the name of Leucothea, Od. 5.333, Hes. Th. 976, Alcm. 84, Pi. O. 2.30, etc. ; prov., Ἰνοῦς ἄχη Zen. 4.38.
ὁ, name of a stream on Delos ; also of a building at its source, IG 11(2).144 A 72 (iv BC).
ακος, ὁ, warden of the Inopos, ib. 142.52, 144 C 10 (iv BC).
ὁ, Arc. for ἔνοικος, IG 5(2).343 (Orchom. Arc., iv BC).
(on the accent v. Hdn. Gr. 1.396), ἰκός, ἡ, worm or grub that destroys the vine-buds, Alcm. 43. (ι, perh. cogn. with ἴψ.)

(ἰξάλη in codd., but ἰξαλῆ Ael. Dion. Fr. 398), ἡ, goat΄s skin (τελείας αἰγὸς δέρμα, Erot.), Hp. Fract. 29, cf. Gal. 19.106 ; used as a dress for actors in satyric dramas, Poll. 4.118. (ἰζάλη Hsch., ἰζάνη Poll. l.c., ἰσάλη Sch. Ar. Nu. 72 ; cf. the forms ἰσσέλα, ἰτθέλα, ἰσθλῆ Hsch., ἰσσέλη Theognost. Can. 14 ; cf. ἴξαλος).

ον, epith. of the Ibex, = τέλειος acc. to Ar.Byz. ap. Eust. 1625.33, or bounding, springing (as Sch. Il., Hsch., etc.), or = τομίας (as Porph. ap. Sch. Il.), ἰξάλου αἰγὸς ἀγρίου Il. 4.105, cf. AP 6.32 (Agath.), 113 (Simm.), 9.99 (Leon.). (Perh. borrowed fr. Asia Minor.)
ατος, τό, = aucupium, Gloss.
ῆρος, ὁ, fowler, Man. 4.339.
τό, = aucupium, Gloss.
α, ον, like birdlime, v. ἰξεύτρια.

οῦ, ὁ, fowler, birdcatcher, Lyc. 105, LXX Am. 8.1, AP 9.824 (Eryc.), Cat.Cod.Astr. 1.166, Apollod. Poliorc. 152.2, Porph. Abst. 1.53 ; ἰ. κῶρος Bion Fr. 9. as Adj., catching with birdlime, ἰ. κάλαμοι AP 6.152 (Agis).
ή, όν, of an ἰξευτής, Artem. 2.19 ; τὰ Ἰ., title of lost poem by Opp. ; ἡ ἰξευτική (sc. τέχνη) Poll. 7.139.
ἡ, fem. of ἰξευτήρ, epith. of Τύχη, Plu. 2.322f ; — written ἰξευτηρία, ib. 281e (s.v.l.).
(< ἰξός) catch by birdlime, Artem. 2.19, EM 471.53 ; — Med., Poll. 7.135.

ἡ, = ἰξός 1, Thphr. HP 3.16.1, CP 2.17.1, prob. in Dsc. 3.89. = χαμαιλέων λευκός, pine-thistle, Atractylis gummifera, Dsc. 3.8, Plin. HN 22.45 ; ἡ ἰ. ἡ ἐν Κρήτῃ Thphr. HP 9.1.3. = ἰξίας, Sch. Nic. Al. 279. = κιρσός, varicocele, Arist. HA 518b25, Pr. 878b37, Plu. 2.202b.
ου, ὁ, = χαμαιλέων μέλας, chamaeleon-thistle, Cardopatium corymbiferum, Dsc. 3.9, Alex. 21, Gal. 14.140.
ἡ, = ἰξία II, pine-thistle, Atractylis gummifera, Thphr. HP 6.4.3 ; ἄκανθα ἡ ἰ. ib. 9.1.2, al. ; confused with ἑλξίνη by Plin. HN 21.94, 22.41.
εσσα, εν, made from ἰξίας, πῶμα Nic. Al. 279.
τό, leaf of χαμαιλέων λευκός (= ἰξία II), Gal. 19.106.
ὁ, epith. of Apollo in Rhodes, from a place Ἰξίαι, Artem. ap. St.Byz. s. h. v.

Ion. ἴξις, εως, ἡ, (< ἵκω) coming, E. Tr. 396 (prob. l.) ; οὐ πτύσις ἀλλ’ ἀναγωγὴ καλέεται, τῆς ἄνω ἴξιος [τῆς ὁδοῦ] τοὔνομα ἔχουσα Aret. SA 2.2 ; οἶνος ὠκὺς ἐς τὴν ἄνω ἴξιν Id. CA 2.4.
passage through, οὐδαμῆ… κατὰ τὴν τοῦ θώρηκος ἴ. Hp. Acut. 15 (but perh. simply, ΄at no point in the θ. ΄)· ἵξιν παρέχεσθαι allow free passage, dub. in Sch. Epicur. Ep. 1 p. 8 U. (fort. εἶξιν).
direction, straight line, esp. vertical line, καθημένῳ πόδες ἐς τὴν ἄνω ἴ. κατ’ ἰθὺ γούνασι his feet when he is seated should be vortically opposite his knees, Hp. Off. 3 ; ἐπιδεῖν δεξιὰ ἐπ’ ἀριστερά, ἀριστερὰ ἐπὶ δεξιά, πλὴν κεφαλῆς· ταύτην δὲ κατ’ ἴξιν vertically, ib. 9 ; βάλλεσθαι χρὴ τὸ ὀθόνιον κατ’ αὐτὴν τὴν ἴ. τοῦ ἕλκεος directly over the wound, Id. Fract. 26 ; τοὺς νάρθηκας… μὴ κατὰ τὴν ἴ. τοῦ ἕλκεος προστιθέναι ibid. ; ὁκόσα κοινωνεῖ τοῖσι τῆς κνήμης ὀστέοισι καὶ αὐτέῃ τῇ ἴξει ib. 9 codd. (κατὰ τὴν ἴξιν Gal. 18(2).423 ; κατ’ αὐτὴν τὴν ἴ. Ermerins). κατ’ ἴξιν c. gen., corresponding to, on the same side as, ἤλγησεν κατὰ βουβῶνα, σπληνὸς κατ’ ἴ., i.e. on the spleen or left side of the body, Hp. Epid. 1.26. γ΄, cf. 4.35, 37, Art. 33, Fract. 16, 18, Mul. 1.17 ; τῶν ὀδόντων τῶν τε ἄνω καὶ τῶν κάτω κατ’ ἴ. Id. Art. 31 ; = ex ipsa parte, Cass.Fel. 37 ; ἐν πυρετοῖσι ἀπὸ σπληνὸς καὶ ἥπατος διὰ ῥινῶν αἱμορραγέουσι, κατ’ ἴ. τοῦ σπλάγχνου τοῦ μυκτῆρος ῥέοντος the nostril corresponding to the organ in question, Aret. SA 2.2 ; ἡ κατ’ ἴ. κληΐς the corresponding (i.e. liver or right side) collarbone, ib. 2.7, cf. CA 1.10 ; κατὰ τὴν ὄπισθεν ἴ. at the back of the leg, Hp. Art. 60. more generally, in line with, κατ’ ἴ. τοῦ πυγαίου ποιησάμενον τὴν σανίδα ib. 75 ; κατ’ ἴ. τῇ ἐντομῇ τῇ ἐς τὸν τοῖχον ib. 47.
ονος, ὁ, Ixion, Pi. P. 2.32, etc. ; perh. connected with ἱκέτης, cf. A. Eu. 441 ; pl., Ἰξίονες tragedies on the subject of I., Arist. Po. 1456a1.
practise bird-liming, οὐκ ἰδίην βολῶν μελέτην AP 9.273 (Bian.).
ον, setting limed twigs ; as Subst., fowler, Man. 4.243.
ον, (< βορά) eating mistletoe-berries, ἡ ἰ. (sc. κίχλη) missel-thrush, Turdus viscivorus, Arist. HA 617a18 ; cf. ἰξοφάγος.
τό, = viscidum, Gloss.
ὁ, one who uses birdlime, fowler, AP 9.264.5 (Apollonid. vel Phil.), 273 tit.
ες, ε, aor. of ἵκω.
Pass., to be smeared with birdlime, Thphr. Ign. 61.
make viscous like birdlime, of a plaster, Paul.Aeg. 2.43.

ὁ, oak-mistletoe, Hozanthus europaeus, Arist. GA 715b30, Dsc. 3.89.
mistletoe-berry, Thphr. CP 2.17.8.
birdlime prepared from the mistletoe-berry, E. Cyc. 433 ; θηρευτὴς ἰ. AP 5.99.
oak-gum, used for the same purpose, Ath. 10.451d, cf. Plu. Cor. 3, Philox. ap. Gal. 13.742.
any sticky substance, Hp. Mul. 1.74, IG1². 314.42 (ἱ-), 2².1673.63. metaph, ἰ. ὀμμάτων of one who causes the eyes to be fixed upon him, Tim.Com. 2 ; ἐκφυγὼν τὸν ἰ. τὸν ἐν πράγματι Luc. Hist. Conscr. 57 ; καθάπερ ἰξῷ τινι προσέχεται τοῖς τοιούτοις ἡ ψυχή Id. Cat. 14.
skinflint, miser, Ar. Fr. 718. (Prob. ϝιξός, cf. Lat. viscum, viscus.)
ον, = ἰξοβόρος, Ath. 2.65a.
έως, ὁ, limed, δόνακες ἰξοφορῆες AP 9.209.

ον, having mistletoe growing thereon, δρύες S. Fr. 403 ; read by Agathocl. in Il. 14.398.
limed, δόναξ Oppian. H. 1.32.
ἡ, = ἰξύς, EM 770.13 ; ἰξύη ib. 636.24.
Adv. from the loins, Arat. 144 ; prob. l. for ἰξυόφιν in Opp. C. 2.6.

ύος, ἡ, waist, of women, περὶ δὲ ζώνην βάλετ’ ἰξυῖ (contr. for ἰξύϊ) Od. 5.231, cf. Longus 1.4 ; of a man, Arat. 310 ; of centaurs, Opp. C. 2.6 ; of a deer, APl. 4.96 ; pl., ἰξύες, οἱ, loins, Hp. Fract. 20, cf. Gal. 19.106 ; sg., = ὀσφύς, [Id.] 14.706. (Perh. akin to ἰσχύς, cf. ἰσχίον.) [υ in nom. and acc. sg., Choerob. in Theod. 1.331 ; υ in trisyll. cases.]
ες, like birdlime, sticky, clammy, Hp. Ulc. 12, Luc. Tim. 29.
τά, festival in honour of Bacchus, Jusj. ap. D. 59.78.
ὁ (sc. μήν), name of month at Astypalaea, IG 12(3).169.15, 170.14 ; at Amorgos, ib. 12(7).67 A 6.

ὁ, Bacchus invoked with the cry of ἰώ, APl. 4.289, Max. 496, Corn. ND 30, Hsch. in pl., worshippers of the God, name of a guild at Athens, SIG 1109.35, al. (ii AD).
hymn beginning with ἰὼ Βάκχε, such as were ascribed to Archilochus, Heph. 15.9.
ου, ὁ, violet-dyer, Gloss.
ές, violetcoloured, Democr. Eph. 1 ; of water, Ath. 2.42e.
Dor. ἰογλέφαρος, ον, violet-eyed, Pi. Fr. 307 ; Χάριτες, Μοῦσαι, B. 18.5, 8.3, cf. Man. 5.145, Luc. Im. 8.

shoot arrows, dart, ARh. 4.1440, AP 5.187 (Leon.) ; ἐς ἐμὴν κραδίην ib. 5.9 (Alc.).
emit poison, Gp. 2.47.12.

ον, (< ἰός) shooting arrows, τόξον AP 6.34 (Rhian.).
shedding venom, venomous, of animals, Numen. ap. Ath. 7.304f, Hdn. 3.9.5 ; Sup., J. AJ 17.5.5 ; ἰοβόλα, τά, venomous animals, Arist. HA 607a28 ; περὶ ἰοβόλων ζῴων, title of work by Philumenus ; τὰ τῶν ἰ. ἄκη Philostr. VA 3.44. of arrows, poisoned, Orph. H. 12.16 ; αἷμα AP 11.237 (Demod.) ; metaph, ἰ. γένυες, of Momus, APl. 4.266.2.

ον, (ἰός²) poison-eating, Opp. C. 3.223 ; of a serpent, διψάς IG 4.620 (Argos).
eating venomously, πυθεδόνες Nic. Th. 467.
ον, dark-haired, Μοῦσαι Pi. I. 7 (6).23.
Dor. for ἰοβλέφαρος.
η, ον, dark-eyed, Hsch.
ον, (< δέω) violet-twined, στέφανοι Pi. Fr. 75.6.
ές, (< δνόφος) dark as the flower ἴον (v. ἴον 1v), purple-dark, εἶρος Od. 4.135, 9.426.

ον, (ἰός¹) holding arrows, φαρέτρη Il. 15.444, Od. 21.12, Pittac. Lyr. 1 ; ἰοδόκη (sc. φαρέτρα), ἡ, quiver, ARh. 2.679, 3.156, 279, AP 6.296 (Leon.), 12.45 (Posidipp.) ; ἰοδόχη, Hsch., Phot.
containing poison, ὀδόντες ἰ. poison-fangs, Nic. Th. 184.
v. ἰοδόκος.
(ἰός²) poisonous, κέντρον Nic. Th. 886 ; λοιγός ib. 243. [Nic. makes ῐ short, as conversely he has ῑάσι from ἴον.]
ές, (< ἴον) like the flower ἴον 1, purple, in Hom. always of the sea, ἰοειδέα πόντον, whether calm or stormy, Il. 11.298, Od. 5.56, 11.107, Hes. Th. 844 ; κρήνη ib. 3.
(ἰός²) poisonous, ἄκανθαι Androm. ap. Gal. 14.38 [who makes ι short; cf. ἰοειδής²].
εσα, εν, (< ἴον) violet-coloured, dark, ἰόεντα σίδηρον Il. 23.850, cf. Phoronis Fr. 2, QS. 6.48 ; ἰόεντα θάλασσαν Nic. Al. 171.
ον, (< ζώνη) with purple girdle, Hsch., dub. in Call. in Stud.Ital. 7 (1929).9.
ές, blooming with violets, στέφανοι Philox. 2.42.
ον, = ἰόζωνος, Alc. 63 (Sapphus est), Sappho Supp. 17.5.
ὁ, = βιόκουρος, Ephes. 3 p. 165.
ον, (ἰός²) born of venom, Procl. H. 1.41.
Ep. for ἴωμεν, 1 pl. pres. subj. of εἶμι (ibo).
ές, (ἰός²) tainted with poison, θηλή AP 9.1 (Polyaen.).
οἱ, twice in Hom., Ἀργεῖοι ἰόμωροι, ἐλεγχέες Il. 4.242 ; Ἀργεῖοι ἰόμωροι, ἀπειλάων ἀκόρητοι 14.479. (Expld. by Sch. as caring for arrows (cf. μέριμνα), but ι is against this ; perh. noisy (cf. ἰά).)

[ῐ], τό, heterocl. dat. pl. ἰάσι [ῑᾰ] Nic. Fr. 74.2 : — violet, Viola odorata, στέφανοι ἴων Sappho Supp. 23.12, cf. Pi. O. 6.55, etc. ; καὶ τὸ ἴον μέλαν ἐντί Theoc. 10.28, cf. AP 4.21 (Mel.) ; κυαναυγές ib. 5.73 (Rufin.) ; ἴ. τὸ μέλαν Thphr. HP 1.13.2, CP 1.13.12 ; ἴον alone, Dsc. 4.121 ; — in Od. 5.72, λειμῶνες μαλακοὶ ἴου ἠδὲ σελίνου θήλεον, there were vv. ll. σίου (Ptol.Euerg.) and θρύου. ἴον τὸ λευκόν (= λευκόϊον) gilliflower, Matthiola incana, Thphr. HP 6.6.3 ; also ἴον alone, ib. 6.8.1. = κρίνον, Philin. ap. Ath. 15.681b. generally, any flower, EM 473.10. a precious stone of dark colour, Plin. HN 37.170. (ϝίον, cf. γία· ἄνθη, Hsch., Lat. viola.)
άδος, ἡ, shaggy, epith. of the wild goat, Od. 14.50.

ὁ, root of a hair, young hair, ἰόνθους ἐκθλιβομένους Phld. Sign. 13, cf. Eun. Hist. p. 250 D., Phryn. PS p. 77 B.
eruption on the face, which often accompanies the first growth of the beard, etc., Hp. Epid. 1.26. β΄, Arist. HA 556b29, Pr. 963b40, Erot. s.v. ὀλοφλυκτίδες ; — hence ἰονθώδης, ες, ἐπάρσεις Thphr. Sud. 16, cf. Gal. 12.824.
ες, v. sub ἴονθος.

α, ον, (< Ἰώ) of or called after Io, epith. of the sea between Epirus and Italy, at the mouth of the Adriatic sea, across which Io swam, πόντιος μυχὸς… Ἰόνιος κεκλήσεται, τῆς σῆς πορείας μνῆμα A. Pr. 840 ; another expl. in Theopomp.Hist. 125 ; Ἰ. κόλπος Hdt. 6.127, Th. 1.24 ; θάλασσα, πόρος, Pi. P. 3.68, N. 4.53 ; also simply ὁ Ἰόνιος Th. 6.30 ; later Ἰόνιον πέλαγος AP 6.251 (Phil.).

Pass., (ἰός³) become or be rusty, Arist. Col. 793b6, Thphr. Char. 10.14, Dsc. 5.78, Antig. Mir. 151.
become acrid, embittered, Hsch. ; — Act. ἰόω, only late, rust, ὁ σίδηρος μᾶλλον ἰοῖ Olymp. in Mete. 266.26, cf. 270.14 ; convert into ἰός, Zos.Alch. pp. 148, 238B.
ον, with violet robe, Hsch.
ον, with dark locks, Μοῖσαι Pi. P. 1.1, cf. Simon. 18.
ον, = ἰοπλόκαμος, Alc. 55 ; κόρα, Νηρήϊδες, B. 8.72, 16.37 ; Μοῖσαι Lyr.Adesp. 53 ; of Apollo, AP 9.524.10.
εως, ἡ, = ἴωσις, Zos.Alch. p. 252B.
μιξόδης, Hsch.
ὁ, v. δορκάς.

ὁ, rust on iron, or verdigris on copper and bronze, Sappho 141 (dub.), Thgn. 451, Pl. R. 609a, Ti. 59c, Theoc. 16.17 ; ἰ. σιδήρου Dsc. 5.80 ; ἰ. χαλκοῦ Hp. Mul. 1.75, Dsc. 5.79, Gal. 12.218 ; patina on bronze statues, ὅπως καθαρὸς ἰοῦ ἔσται ὁ ἀνδριάς SIG 284.15 (Chios, iv BC), cf. Plu. 2.395b. (Perh. identical with ἰός².)

ἴα, ἰόν, one, commonest in fem. (v. εἷς) ; neut. ἰῷ κίον ἤματι Il. 6.422 ; masc. dat. ἰῷ, = ἐκείνῳ, Leg. Gort. 8.8 ; but, = ἑνί, ib. 7.23 ; acc., τόν γ’ ἰὸν ἐνιαυτόν the same year, IG 5(1).1390.126 (Andania, i BC) ; ἰός, = μόνος, acc. to Trypho ap. ADysc. Pron. 56.4.
Boeot. for ἑός.

ὁ, poison, as of serpents, A. Eu. 478, S. Tr. 771, E. Ion 1015, Plu. 2.562c, etc. ; venom of a mad dog, Ruf. Fr. 118 ; ἰὸς ἀμεμφὴς μελισσῶν, of honey with which snakes fed Iamos, Pi. O. 6.47 ; metaph, of envy, A. Ag. 834. (Cf. Skt. viṣám ΄poison΄, Lat. vīrus.)
ὁ, pl. ἰοί, heterocl. ἰά Il. 20.68 (Cypr., acc. to AB 1095) : — arrow, ἰὸν ἕηκε Il. 1.48 ; βλήμενος ἢ ἰῷ ἢ ἔγχεϊ 8.514, cf. A. Pers. 461 ; ἧκεν κομήτην ἰόν S. Tr. 567. (Cf. Skt. íṣ ΄arrow΄.)
τό, sugar of violets, Ruf. Fr. 80.
ον, violet-crowned, epith. of Aphrodite, h.Hom. 6.18, Sol. 19.4 ; of the Muses, Thgn. 250 ; esp. of Athens, Pi. Fr. 76, cf. B. 5.3, Ar. Ach. 637, Eq. 1323.

ητος, ἡ, will, desire, Ep. and Lyr. almost always in dat., θεῶν ἰότητι by the will of the gods, Il. 19.9, Od. 7.214, al., cf. Alc. 13A ; μητρὸς ἐμῆς ἰότητι at her will, Il. 18.396 ; κακῆς ἰ. γυναικός Od. 11.384 ; μνηστήρων ἰ. 18.234 ; ἀλλήλων ἰ. Il. 5.874 ; ἀναιδήτῳ ἰ. with shameless will, ARh. 4.360 ; acc. only in Il. 15.41 δι’ ἐμὴν ἰ. once in Trag., for the sake of, ἰότατι γάμων A. Pr. 558 (lyr.). — Hsch. explains it by βουλήσει, αἰτία, ὀργῇ, χάριτι.
ον, (ἰός²) poison-bearing, venomous, Opp. C. 3.73.
ές, (ἰός¹) arrow-stricken, AP 5.86 (Rufin.), 9.265 (Apollonid. or Phil.).

or ἰοῦ (v. sub fin.), Interj., a loud cry expressive of sorrow, joy, or surprise, of grief of annoyance, usu. twice repeated, ἰοὺ ἰού D. 19.209 ; ἰ. ἰ. δύστηνος or δύστηνε, S. Tr. 1143, OT 1071 ; ἰ. ἰ. βοᾶν, κεκραγέναι, Ar. Nu. 543, Pax 345 ; c. gen., ἰ. ἰ. τῶν… κιγκλίδων Jul. Caes. 330d ; rarely once, φῦ (φεῦ codd.), ἰ. τῆς ἀσβόλου Ar. Th. 245 ; or thrice, Id. Pax 110 ; with other Interj., ἰ. ἰ. ὢ ὢ κακά A. Ag. 1214 ; ἰ. ἰ. πόπαξ Id. Eu. 143 (lyr.). of joyful surprise, hallo!, hurrah!, Id. Ag. 25, E. Cyc. 464, 576, Ar. Eq. 1096, Pl. R. 432d, Grg. 499b, Smp. 223a. (Sch. Ar. Pax 345, 316 says that ἰοὺ ἰού is of woe, ἰοῦ ἰοῦ of joy ; the rule is not observed in codd. In Att. Poets it sts. stands extra versum, A. Ag. 25, Ar. Nu. 1.)
side with or imitate the Jews, LXX Es. 8.17, Ep. Gal. l.c..
ή, όν, Jewish, LXX 2 Ma. 8.11, etc. Adv. -κῶς J. BJ 6.1.3, Ep. Gal. 2.14, Cod.Just. 1.1.7.4.
ὁ, a Jew ; Ἰουδαία, a Jewess ; ἡ Ἰουδαία (sc. γῆ) Judaea.
ὁ, Judaism, LXX 2 Ma. 2.21, Ep. Gal. 1.13.
in the Hebrew tongue, LXX 4Ki. 18.26.
πεπόρευται, Hsch.
ὁ (sc. μήν), name of month in Lesbos (?), CIG 6850 A ; in Cyprus, Cat.Cod.Astr. 2.139 ; — also Ἰουλίηος, CIG 2827, 2836 (Aphrodisias) ; Ἰούλιος, = Lat. Julius, Hemerolog.Flor.
become downy or hairy, Tryph. 53, cf. Phot.
v. sub Ἰουλαῖος.
v. sub Ἰουλαῖος.
ίδος, ἡ, rainbow-wrasse, Coris iulis, Arist. HA 610b6, AP 7.504.5 (Leon.), Numen. ap. Ath. 7.304f, Artem. 1.14.
ον, (ἴουλος IV) footed like the centipede, i.e. manyfooted, many-oared, of a ship, Lyc. 23.

ὁ, down, the first growth of the whiskers and beard, in pl., πρίν σφωϊν ὑπὸ κροτάφοισιν ἰούλους ἀνθῆσαι Od. 11.319 ; later in sg., στείχει δ’ ἴ. ἄρτι διὰ παρηΐδων A. Th. 534 ; πρᾶτον ἴ. ἀπὸ κροτάφων καταβάλλειν Theoc. 15.85 ; ἔτι χνοάοντας ἰούλους ἀντέλλων ARh. 2.43 ; ὑπὸ κροτάφοισιν ἰούλους κειράμενος AP 6.198 (Antip. Thess.) ; ἰούλοις πλῆσαι παρειάς IG 14.1601.
corn-sheaf, whence Demeter is said to be named Ἰουλώ, Semus 19, Carm.Pop. 1.
song in honour of Demeter, Semus l.c., Apollod. Hist. 149 J., Eratosth. Fr. 10.
catkin, Thphr. HP 3.5.5, 3.7.3 ; tendril, ib. 3.18.11.
IV, creature like the centipede, prob. the wood-louse, Arist. HA 523b18, PA 682b3, Thphr. Sign. 19, Arat. 959 ; earthworm, Numen. ap. Ath. 7.305a. = ἰουλίς, Eratosth. Fr. 12 (pl.). (Perh. cogn. with οὖλος)
ον, downy, γένυς Demitsas Μακεδ. No.410 (Thessalonica, ii AD).
ες, scolopendra-like, Arist. PA 682a5.
οῦς, ἡ, goddess of sheaves, epith. of Demeter, Semus 19 ; cf. ἴουλος II.
prob. corrupt in A. Supp. 828 ; interj. expressing aversion, acc. to Sch.
ον, (ἰός², φέρω) poison-bearing, Opp. C. 3.433.

ἡ, (ἰός¹) arrow-pourer, shooter of arrows, epith. of Artemis, Il. 5.53, etc. ; ἰ. παρθένος Pi. P. 2.9 ; as Subst., Ἰοχέαιρα Il. 21.480, Od. 11.198, Schwyzer 758 (vi BC), IG 14.1389i53 ; later ἰ. φαρέτρα AP 6.9 (Mnasalc.).
ΙI. (ἰός²) poison-shedding, of serpents, Nic. Fr. 33. (-χέϝαιρα from χέω, not as expld. by Apollon.Soph. Lex. etc. from χαίρω.) [ι as in ἰός ; yet ι in Pi. l.c.]
τά, name of a festival, perh. Parilia (parelia, pardia codd.), Gloss.
κάμνη, Hsch.
Aeol. for ὕπαρ, Jo. Gramm. Comp. 3.15.
γαστήρ (Tarent.), Hsch.
οῦ, ὁ, = furnarius, Gloss. ; prob. for ἰπνίτης in AP 6.299 (Phan.).
(< ἰπνός) dry or bake in the oven, Hsch., prob. in IG1². 4.15 (hιπν-).
ἡ, woodpecker, Ant.Lib. 21.6 ; cf. ἴππα (ἵπτα cod.) ; = δρυοκόλαψ, Hsch. ; ἰπνή· ἐφιππίς (Sicel), Id.
τό, Dim. of ἰπνός, Dieuch. ap. Orib. 4.5.2.
α, ον, (ἰπνός 1) of an oven ; — hence ἴπνια, τά, soot, Hsch., cf. Sch. Ar. V. 832. (ἰπνός IV) of a dunghill, Call. Fr. 216.
ου, ὁ, baked in the oven, οἱ ἰ. ἄρτοι Hp. Vict. 2.42, Polem.Hist. 86, IG 5(1).363.18 (Sparta, i AD ; written -είταν) ; without ἄρτος, Timocl. 33 ; ἰ. φθοΐς AP 6.299 (Phan., sed leg. -ευτής).
τὴν φρυγίαν (Cret.), Hsch.
ές, (< καίω) baked in the oven, Luc. Lex. 6.
= furnarius, Gloss. (also ἰπνοκαύτης, ibid.).
φρύγιον, οἱ δὲ τὴν ὑπόκαυσιν τοῦ ἰπνοῦ, Hsch.
ητος, ὁ, boiler, cauldron, Luc. Lex. 8, Ath. 3.98c.
τό, Dim. of ἰπνολέβης, Poll. 10.66.
τό, mare΄s-tail, Hippuris vulgaris, Thphr. HP 4.10.1.
later for ἰπνοπλάθος.
ὁ, (< πλάσσω) oven-maker, fire-clay moulder, worker in terra-cotta, much like κοροπλάθος, Pl. Tht. 147a ; — later ἰπνοπλάθης, Poll. 7.163, Tim. Lex., Harp.
ου, ὁ, = ἰπνοπλάθος, Gal. Thras. 43.
όν, = ἰπνοπλάθος, Luc. Prom. Es 2, Them. Or. 21.256d.

ὁ, I. oven, furnace, Hdt. 5.92. ηʹ, Hp. Morb. 2.47, Antiph. 176.4, Diph. Siph. ap. Ath. 2.54a, Archestr. Fr. 46 ; esp. for heating water for the bath, Ar. V. 139, Av. 437.
II. the place of the oven, i.e. the kitchen, Semon. 7.61, Ar. V. 837, Lycurg. Fr. 73.
III. lantern, Ar. Pax 841, Pl. 815, SIG 1027.13 (Cos, 1v/iii BC), Ael. NA 2.8.
IV. = κοπρών, dunghill, privy, Ar. Fr. 353, Hsch. (Prob. cogn. with Engl. oven.)
ῶνος, ὁ, kitchen, IG 11(2).287 A 147, al. (Delos, iii BC).
ον, (< ἴψ) killing the worms in vines, epith. of Heracles at Erythrae, Str. 13.1.64.

ἡ (so in Pi. O. 4.8) or τό (Eust. 844.39), in a mouse-trap, the piece of wood that falls and catches the mouse, Ar. Pl. (815?) ap. Poll. 10.155, Id. 7.41, Eust. 16.40, etc. cf. εἶπος.
any weight, fuller΄s press, Archil. 169 ; ἶ. ἀνεμόεσσα, of Aetna as the weight which holds Typhoeus down, Pi. O. 4.8 ; press used in surgery, Hp. Mochl. 38. (Perh. cf. ἴπτομαι.)

press, squeeze, Cratin. 91 ; esp. in surgery, Hp. Art. 47 ; ἰ. τὴν κεφαλὴν τοῦ βραχίονος Heliod. ap. Orib. 49.13.8 ; — Pass., to be weighed down, ἰπούμενος ῥίζαισιν Αἰτναίαις ὕπο A. Pr. 365 ; ἰπούμενος ταῖς ἐσφοραῖς Ar. Eq. 924.

ῶν, οἱ, (< ἀγρέω) three officers at Lacedaemon, who chose 300, the flower of the ἔφηβοι, to serve as a body-guard for the kings (v. ἱππεύς II. 1), X. HG 3.3.9, Lac. 4.3, Archyt. ap. Stob. 4.1.138 ; sg., Th. 4.38 (unless it be pr. n.).
ὁ, = ἵππος ἄγριος, wild horse, Opp. C. 3.252.

όν, carrying horses ; esp. of ships used as cavalry transports, πλοῖα Hdt. 6.48 ; νέες ib. 95 ; ναῦς Th. 2.56, 4.42, Arr. An. 2.19.1 ; τριήρεις D. 4.16, DS. 11.3 ; ἱππαγωγοί alone, Ar. Eq. 599, D. 4.21 ; Ἱππαγωγός as pr. n. of a ship, IG2². 1623.14.

Dor. fut. 3 sg. ἱππασεῖται Dialex. 6.4 : — drive horses, drive a chariot, Ἀντίλοχ΄, ἀφραδέως ἱππάζεαι Il. 23.426 ; later, ride, Hdt. 4.114, Hp. Aër. 17, Ar. Nu. 15, etc. ; ἱ. ἐφ’ ἵππων Hdt. 4.110 ; ἵππῳ X. Eq. 10.1 ; metaph, ἁξυσμὰ ἐκ ποδὸς εἰς κεφαλὰν ἱππάζεται Sophr. 53 ; — rare in Act., ἱππάσαι πῶλον ap. Poll. 1.182. Pass., of the horse, to be ridden or driven, Pl. Ion 540e ; to be broken in for riding, X. Eq. 3.1. c. acc. loci, ἱππάζεσθαι χώραν ride over a country, Plu. Cam. 23 ; τὰς ὁδούς DS. 13.88.
ἡ, v. sub ἴπνη ; as pr. n. Ἵππα, Hippa, nurse of Dionysus, Orph. H. 48.4.
ΐδος, ἡ, hyperdor. for ἱππηΐς, fem. of ἱππικός I. 3, of a knight, πόρπα, i.e. fibula which fastened the trabea of a Roman eques, Epigr.Gr. 985.1 (Philae).
ἡ, cavalry-action, Sch. Pi. N. 1.23 (pl.).
ον, fighting on horseback, equestrian, Pi. N. 1.17.

ἡ, mare΄s-milk cheese, used by the Scythians, Hp. Aër. 18, A. Fr. 198, Theopomp.Hist. 48, Thphr. HP 9.13.2, Dsc. 2.71 ; — also ἱππάκης, ου, ὁ, Eust. 916.16.
2. horse΄s rennet, Dsc. 2.75.
ΙI. a leguminous plant, Ph.Mech. Bel. 86.25, Plin. HN 25.83.
ου, ὁ, v. ἱππάκη I.
οῦ, ὁ, mounted javelineer, Ael. Tact. 2.13, Arr. An. 4.4.7, Poll. 1.131.
τό, (cf. ἄκοπος) remedy for horses, Hippiatr. 130.
όνος, ὁ, horsecock, gryphon, a fabulous animal in A. Fr. 134, cf. Ar. Ra. 932, Av. 800.
α, ον, poet. for ἱππικός, Opp. C. 1.169, 242, etc.
ὁ, name of the monsoon in the Indian Ocean (from the name of the pilot who observed it), prob. in Peripl. M.Rubr. 57.
ου, ὁ, mounted man, PLond. 1821.80.
ὁ, centaur, Gal. UP 3.1, Eust. 1909.53.
a cry of the Ἱππεῖς, a parody of the boatmen΄s cry (ῥυππαπαῖ), Ar. Eq. 602.

τό, Dim. of ἵππος, pony, PCair. Zen. 30, al. (iii BC), Arr. Tact. 19.3.
wretched horse, in contempt, X. Cyr. 1.4.19, Plu. Phil. 7, Them. Or. 24.306d.
statuette of a horse, IG 11(2).203 B 84 (Delos, iii BC).
οῦ, ὁ, Laced. for ἵππαρχος, commander of cavalry, X. HG 4.44.10, 5.12 ; cf. ἵπφαρμος.
τό, head-quarters of the ἵππαρχος, IG2². 895 (ii BC).

to be ἵππαρχος, command cavalry, c. gen., τῆς ἵππου Hdt. 9.20, 69 ; ἱππαρχηκὼς ἀνδρῶν καλῶν κἀγαθῶν Din. 3.12 ; ἱππέων D. 21.164 ; abs., X. Ages. 2.4, Lys. 26.20, D. 21.172 ; οἱ ἱππαρχηκότες Hyp. Lyc. 17 ; of the Roman magister equitum and praefectus equitum, DC. 43.48, App. BC 5.8 ; — Pass., serve under an ἵππαρχος, Arist. Pol. 1277b10.

Dor. ἱππάρχας, Ion. gen. ἱππάρχεω IG 12(8).194.7 (Samothrace), Michel 596 (Cyzicus), ὁ, = ἵππαρχος, OGI 217 (Caria, iii BC, pl.), Plb. 10.22.6 (Achaean), 18.22.2 (Macedonian), cf. LXX 2Ki. 1.6, PTeb. 54.2 (i BC), Plu. Tim. 32 ; at Sparta, IG 5(1).32A, al. ; = Lat. magister equitum, Plb. 3.87.9, DH. 5.75, Nic.Dam. 130.17J., etc. ; = praefectus equitum, App. BC 2.102 ; = praefectus alae, J. BJ 2.14.5.

ἡ, office of ἵππαρχος, X. Ath. 1.3 (pl.) ; of the magister equitum, DC. Fr. 36.26, Lyd. Mag. 2.13.
a squadron of horse such as he commands, Plb. 10.23.4, DS. 17.57, Str. 17.1.12, Plu. Eum. 7, Arr. An. 1.24.3 ; consisting of 512 men, Ascl.Tact. 7.11, etc.
ή, όν, of or for a ἵππαρχος, ἡγεμονία ἱ., = ἱππαρχία, Suid. s.v. ἵππαρχος ; ἱ. ἐστί it is part of his duty, X. Eq. Mag. 5.1 ; ἱππαρχικός, ὁ (sc. λόγος), title of treatise by Xenophon.

ὁ, ruling the horse, epith. of Poseidon, Pi. P. 4.45.
commander of cavalry, τῆς ἵππου Hdt. 7.154 ; at Athens, IG2². 116.15 (iv BC), Ar. Av. 799, Lys. 16.8, Pl. Lg. 755c, 880d, X. Eq. Mag. 1.7, al. ; ἵ. εἰς Λῆμνον χειροτονεῖν Hyp. Lyc. 17, cf. D. 4.26 ; in other states, Th. 4.72, IG 7.2466 (Thebes, iii BC), etc. ; in the Achaean league, ib. 5(2).344.7 (Orchomenus), etc. ; = Lat. magister equitum, DS. 12.64, Plu. Cam. 5, etc. ; = praefectus equitum, App. Hisp. 47 ; cf. ἱππάρχης.

άδος, ἡ, pecul. fem. of ἱππικός, ἱ. στολή a riding-dress, Hdt. 1.80 ; = Lat. equester, ἱ. ἐσθής DC. 38.14.
as Subst., ἡ ἱ. (sc. τάξις) the order of knights (< ἱππεῖς) at Athens, Arist. Pol. 1274a21 ; θυσίαι, βοῦς ἱππάδες of sacrifices offered by the knights, Hsch. ; πύλαι ἱ., name of a gate at Athens, Plu. 2.849c.
knights’ tax, ἱππάδα τελεῖν Is. 7.39, Arist. Ath. 7.4, Plu. Sol. 18 ; θητικοῦ ἀντὶ τέλους ἱππάδ’ ἀμειψάμενος Epigr. ap. Arist. Ath. l.c.
at Rome, = ordo equester, DC. 40.57, al. ; in full ἡ ἱ. τάξις Hdn. 5.1.5.
a boy΄s game, Poll. 9.122.
= ἵππος, ἡ, mare, Opp. C. 1.162, Hippiatr. 14, BGU 21iii 8 (iv AD).

ἡ, riding, horse-exercise, Ar. Ach. 1165 (lyr.) ; ἱ. ποιεῖσθαι, = ἱππάζεσθαι, to take a ride, X. Eq. 8.9, cf. An. 2.5.33 ; ἱ. ἱππάσασθαι Id. Oec. 11.17 ; horsemanship, Id. An. 2.5.33 ; as a subject of competition, IG 7.3087 (Lebad.).
chariot-driving, Luc. DDeor. 12.1, etc.
cavalry, Arr. An. 4.4.7.

η, ον, fit for horses, fit for riding, Αἴγυπτον τὸ πρὶν ἐοῦσαν ἱππασίμην καὶ ἁμαξευομένην, opp. ἄνιππος, Hdt. 2.108, cf. 5.63, 9.13, X. Cyr. 1.4.14, Aen.Tact. 6.6, Plb. 10.49.5, Onos. 31.1, etc. ; τὸ ἱππάσιμον, i.e. τὸ πεδινόν, X. HG 7.2.12 ; τὰ ἱ. τῆς χώρας ἄνιππα ποιεῖν Aen.Tact. 8.4 ; metaph, τοῖς κόλαξιν ἑαυτὸν ἀνεικὼς ἱππάσιμον allowing himself to be ridden by flatterers, Plu. Alex. 23.
τό, Dim. of ἵππος, Theognost. Can. 125.
ατος, τό, a ride, Ach.Tat. 1.13.
ὁ, riding, Sch. E. Hel. 1355.
ῆρος, ὁ, = ἱππαστής, metaph of the μύωψ, AP 5.202 (Asclep.) ; κημός ib. 7.424 (Antip.Sid.).
οῦ, ὁ, = ἱππευτής, Luc. Am. 46. as Adj., fit for riding, of a horse, X. Eq. 10.17.
Adv. like a horseman, καθίζειν Hsch.
ή, όν, fond of riding, Plu. Alc. 23.
ή, όν, that can be ridden, Arist. HA 576b17.
κάμηλοι, αἱ, dromedaries, Plu. Eum. 15.
εως, ἡ, starting-post in a race-course, Plb. Fr. 52 (pl.), Abh.Berl.Akad. 1904 (2).9 (Pap., ii BC), DH. 3.68 (pl.), Epigr. ap. Paus. 6.20.14 (Olymp.), prob. in SIG 251 H ii63, 253 U (Delph., iv BC)
τά, = ἱππάφεσις, Tab. Defix. Aud. 234.21 (Carthage, i AD).
caballi ammissi, carceres, Gloss. (prob. ἱππαφέσεις).

ἡ, (< ἱππεύω) riding or driving of horses, horsemanship, racing, S. El. 505 (lyr.) ; pl., E. HF 374 (lyr.).
cavalry, X. An. 5.6.8, Ages. 1.23.
breed of horses, ἐνδόξου γενομένης ἐνθένδε ἱ. Str. 5.1.9.

α, ον, (< ἵππος) of a horse or horses, ζυγόν, φάτνη, Il. 5.799, 10.568 ; κάπαι Od. 4.40 ; ἵ. λόφος horse-hair crest, Il. 15.537 ; ἔντεα Pi. N. 9.22 ; γένος, μάνδραι, S. Ant. 341 (lyr.), Fr. 659.3 ; ἔθειραι Theoc. 16.81 ; τὸ ἵππειον [γάλα] Arist. HA 522a28, Posidon. ap. Gal. 19.712 ; κάλω ἱππείω δύο IG1². 330.19. Adv. -είως Dam. Pr. 58. ἵππειος, ὁ (sc. μήν), name of month at Thronion, Klio 16.176 (Delph.). (ἵππιος is the usual form in Trag., ἱππικός in Prose.)
fem. of ἱππελάτης, Orph. H. 32.12.
ου, ὁ, driver or rider of horses, Opp. C. 1.95.
ὁ, lit., horse-deer, perh. nylghau, Portax picta, Arist. HA 498b32 ; ἡ θήλεια ἱ. οὐκ ἔχει κέρατα ib. 499b2.
οῦ, ὁ, lover of horses, Ael. NA 2.28.
ὁ, horse-fever, formed after ἴκτερος, ὕδερος, etc., with a pun on ἔρος (= ἔρως), Ar. Nu. 74.
ατος, τό, ride on horseback or journey in a chariot, E. IT 1428 ; [Νύξ], μακρὸν ἵ. διώκεις Id. Fr. 114 (lyr.).

gen. έως (-έω dub. in Hsch.), Ep. ῆος, ὁ, (< ἵππος) one who fights from a chariot, Hom. (only in Il.), opp. πεζός, 2.810 ; either of the driver or of the hero who fights, 12.66, 15.270 ; also of one who drives in a chariot-race, 23.262.
horseman, rider, cavalryman, ἰππήων στρότος Sappho Supp. 5.1, cf. Hdt. 3.88, 9.49, A. Pers. 14 (anap.), Arist. Pol. 1270a29, etc. ; τῆς πολιτείας ἱ. a public courier, Aristaenet. 1.26.
groom, Class. Rev. 27.12 (Laodicea Combusta), 24.12, JHS 18.108 (near Lysias). ἱππεῖς, in social and political sense, knights, forming an aristocracy in early Greek communities, Arist. Pol. 1297b18, etc. ; at Eretria, ib. 1306a35, Ath. 15.2 ; at Sparta, a royal bodyguard, Hdt. 8.124, cf. 1.67, etc. ; esp. at Athens, the Second Class in Solon΄s constitution, Arist. Ath. 7.3 ; later, an aristocratic corps of cavalry, Ar. Eq. 225, And. 3.5, Philoch. 100, etc. of the Roman equites, DS. 37.8, DH. 4.24, App. BC 1.22, etc. ; ἱππεὺς Ῥωμαίων, = Lat. eques Romanus, Mon.Anc.Gr. 7.17, IG 3.768a, IGRom. 3.204 (Ancyra), OGI 547.2 (ibid.), 645.7 (Palmyra), prob. in IGRom. 4.1213 (Thyatira).
nimble kind of crab, Arist. HA 525b8. kind of comet, Plin. HN 2.90, Lyd. Ost. 11.
girl΄s ornament, Hsch., cf. Ostr. 323 (ii BC). a measure, πυρῶν, ἀμυγδάλων, ἀλεύρων, Supp.Epigr. 2.710 (Pednelissus).
εως, ἡ, riding, in pl., Sch. E. Ph. 791.
ῆρος, ὁ, = ἱππευτής, πῶλος, ἱ. πεδίων, οὐχ ἁλός AP 9.295 (Bianor).
οῦ, ὁ, rider, horseman, Pi. P. 9.123 ; as Adj., Τρῶες B. 12.160 ; στρατός E. HF 408 (lyr.).

to be a horseman or rider, ride, Hdt. 1.136, etc. ; ἱ. ταῖς κυούσαις ἵπποις Arist. HA 576a21 ; ἱ. ἐπ’ ὄνου Luc. Bacch. 2 ; of a people, ἱππεύει ταῦτα τὰ ἔθνη Hdt. 7.84, cf. 87 ; — also in Med., Id. 1.27, 79. metaph, of the wind, ζεφύρου πνοαῖς ἱππεύσαντος E. Ph. 212 (lyr.) ; σελάνα ἱππεύουσα δι’ ὀρφναίας Id. Supp. 994 (lyr.) ; also, rush, πρὸς φόνον Id. HF 1001.
serve in the cavalry, Lys. 14.7, X. HG 3.1.4, Pl. Lg. 756b, etc. at Rome, to be an eques, DC. 49.12 ; τὸ -εῦον the ordo equester, Id. 60.7. of a horse, as we say ΄the horse rides (i.e. carries his rider) well΄, X. Eq. 1.6, 3.4, 10.3.
drive a team, Ar. Nu. 1406.
ου, ὁ, driver of horses, of Poseidon, Lyc. 767.
όν, (ἄγω) = ἱππαγωγός, νῆες (expressed or understood) Philoch. 132, Plb. 1.27.9, DS. 20.83 ; τριήρης Ἱππηγός as pr. n., IG2². 1628.423, 1629.944.

Adv. like a horse, A. Th. 328 (lyr.), Supp. 431 (lyr.).
like a horseman, Ar. Pax 81.
ἡ, (< ἐλαύνω) driving or riding of horses, Hld. 8.14, Them. Or. 15.188a, 18.216d.
α, ον, fit for riding or driving, ἱ. ὁδός chariot-road, Il. 7.340.
ride or drive, Ar. Av. 1443.

ου, ὁ, driver of horses, one who fights from a chariot, Hom. (always in Ep. from ἱππηλάτα, and only in nom.), as an epith. of honour, Knight, ἱ. Τυδεύς, γέρων ἱ. Πηλεύς, Φοῖνιξ, Οἰνεύς, Il. 4.387, 7.125, 9.432, 581 ; Νέστωρ Od. 3.436 ; generally ἱππηλάται E. Rh. 117 ; as Adj., ἱ. λεώς, opp. πεδοστιβής, A. Pers. 126 (lyr.).

ον, fit for horsemanship or driving, νῆσος Od. 4.607 ; γαῖα 13.242 ; ὁδὸς ἱ. chariot-road, Luc. Rh. Pr. 3, Poll. 9.37 ; ἱ. οἶδμα Nonn. D. 20.157 ; θάλασσα Agath. 4.29, cf. 5.11 ; ἱ. ἔργον Ἀθήνης, i.e. the Trojan horse, Tryph. 2 ; τὸ δι’ ἡδονῆς καθάπερ ἱ. τι χωρίον Porph. Marc. 6.
ἡ, milking of mares, Scymn. 855 (pl.).
οι, (< ἀμέλγω) the Mare-milkers, a Scythian or Tartar tribe, Il. 13.5, cf. Str. 7.3.2 ; Σκύθαι ἱ. Hes. Cat. Oxy. 1358 Fr. 2.15 ; ἱ. Κιμμέριοι Call. Dian. 252.
ape Hippias, Philostr. VS 2.21.3.
ακτος, ὁ, king of horsemen, A. Pers. 996 (lyr.).
ου, ὁ, = ἱππεύς IV, Apul. ap. Lyd. Mens. 4.7.
ή, όν, of or for farriery ; ἱππιατρικόν, τό, a work on farriery, Suid. s.v. Χείρων ; ἱππιατρικά, τά, title of extant compilation ; also ἱππιατρικόν, τό, tax on farriers, PHib. 1.45.21 (iii BC).
(on the accent v. Hdn. Gr. 1.229), ὁ, veterinary surgeon, farrier, IG 9(2).69.5 (ii BC), PGen. 42.35 (iii AD), Hippiatr. 12, etc. ; cf. ἱπποϊατρός.
τό, a kind of fish, Epich. 44.

ή, όν, (< ἵππος) of a horse or horses, freq. in Trag., ἱ. ἐκ πλευμόνων A. Th. 61 ; ἱ. φρυάγματα ib. 245, cf. S. El. 717, 719 ; ὀχήματα, ἄντυγες, ib. 740, Aj. 1030 ; φάτναι E. Ba. 509.
of horsemen or chariots, ἀγών Hdt. 1.167, And. 4.26 (pl.) ; in ἱππικῶν ἀγών S. El. 698, ἱππικῶν is prob. neut. (v. infr. iv) ; δρόμος ib. 754 ; ναυάγια ib. 730 ; ἆθλον Pl. Lg. 949a. = Lat. equester, τάξις, ἀξίωμα, DH. 12.1, Plu. Pomp. 23 ; of persons, of equestrian rank, ἱ. ἄνδρες Str. 3.4.20, cf. IGRom. 3.474 (Lycia, iii AD), etc.
of riding or horsemanship, equestrian, X. HG 5.3.20 ; ἱ. ἄσκησις training in horsemanship, IG2². 1042.21, al. ; ἱ. ἡγήτωρ leader of the knights, ib. 3.693 ; skilled in riding, opp. ἄφιππος, Pl. Prt. 350a, al. ; Comp., Satyr. 1, Phld. Mus. p. 6 K. ; Sup., Arr. Tact. 16.9. ἡ ἱππική (sc. τέχνη), horsemanship, riding, Ar. Nu. 27, etc. ; περὶ κῆς, title of treatise by Xenophon ; ἱ. ἐπιστήμη Pl. La. 193b ; ἱ. λόγοι X. HG 5.3.20 ; τὰ ἱ. [πράγματα] Pl. Alc. 1.124e, cf. Thg. 126a ; ἡ ἐμὴ ἱ. this riding of mine, Lys. 24.10.
fit for riding, Sup. -ώτατον, χρῆμα γυνή Ar. Lys. 677. τὸ ἱ. the horse, cavalry, Hdt. 7.87, E. Supp. 682, X. An. 6.5.29, etc. ; τὰ ἱ. Plb. 3.114.5.
course or space of four stadia, Plu. Sol. 23. the circus at Rome, Tab. Defix. Aud. 187.59. Adv. -κῶς like a horseman ; Sup. -κώτατα with best horsemanship, X. Oec. 21.7.

α, ον, (< ἵππος) poet. form of ἵππειος, of a horse or horses, λόφοι crests of horsehair, Alc. 15.2 ; σθένος ἵ. Pi. P. 2.12 ; Ἄργος ἵ. (cf. ἱππόβοτος) Id. I. 7 (6).11, B. 18.15 ; δρομεύς, prob. l. in E. El. 825 ; ἄνασσαἱ.
Queen of the Amazons, Id. Hipp. 307 ; epith. of Poseidon as creator of the horse, B. 16.99, A. Th. 130 (lyr.), Ar. Eq. 551, Nu. 83, IG1². 310.142, etc. ; hence, of Colonos as sacred to him, Arg. S. OC, Paus. 1.30.4 (but cf. Pherecr. 134) ; also of Athena, Pi. O. 13.82, S. OC 1070 (lyr.), Harp. ; of Hera, at Olympia, Paus. 5.15.5 ; of Ares, Id. 5.15.6, cf. Tryph. 105.
of horsemen or the horse-race, ἵ. νόμος Pi. O. 1.101 ; ἱππίαν ἔσοδον Id. P. 6.50 ; ἄεθλα AP 6.312 (Anyte) ; sc. ἀγών SIG 1064.8 (Halic., i BC). Ἵππιος, ὁ (sc. μήν), month at Rhegium, IG 14.612.
ου, ὁ, shaggy with horsehair, λόφος Il. 6.469.
ου, ὁ, one who fights from a chariot, 24.257, Od. 11.259, Hes. Fr. 7 ; later, horseman, rider, A. Pers. 29 (anap.). as Adj., ἱ. κλόνοι the tumult of the horse-fight, ib. 105 ; cf. ἱπποχάρμης.

ὁ, Dim. of ἵππος, name of a play by Alexis, Ath. 3.120b.
small statue of a horse, Michel 832.41 (Samos, iv BC).
an ornament for the head (cf. ἱππεύς v), Cratin.Jun. 5, Hsch.
Adv., = ἱππηδόν, astride, Ἀφροδίτη ἱ. καθημένη ἐπὶ Ψυχῆς PMagPar. 1.1724.
ἱπποφορβός, Hsch.
ῶνος, ὁ (sc. μήν), month at Eretria, IG 11(4).1066b21 (found in Delos).

ον, gen. ονος, (< βαίνω) going on horseback, equestrian, Ἀριμασπὸν ἱπποβάμονα στρατόν A. Pr. 805 ; στρατὸς ἱ., of centaurs, S. Tr. 1095.
trotting like a horse, or used for riding, κάμηλοι A. Supp. 284 (cj. Turneb.).
metaph, ῥήματα ἱ. high-paced words, bombast, fustian, Ar. Ra. 821.
ου, ὁ, horseman, A. Pers. 26 (anap.). ἱ. ἵππος or ὄνος, stallion, Str. 8.8.1, Hippiatr. 14 ; cf. ἱπποβότης.
ὁ, (< βινέω) comic distortion of the pr. n. Ἱππόνικος, = ἱππόπορνος, Ar. Ra. 433.
τό, horses’ keep, Theognost. Can. 125.
όν, (< βόσκω) feeding horses, Ael. NA 6.10, Suid., Gloss.

ου, ὁ, (< βόσκω) feeder of horses, Ἀτρεύς E. Or. 1000 (lyr., but prob. -βώτα), IA 1059 (but prob. -βάτας). ἱπποβόται, οἱ, at Chalcis in Euboea a social class (cf. ἱππεύς II), Knights, Hdt. 5.77, 6.100 ; ἡ ἱπποβοτῶν πολιτεία Arist. Fr. 603.

ον, (< βόσκω) grazed by horses, Od. 4.606, E. Andr. 1229 (anap.), IG1². 1034, Just. Nov. 25.1 ; ἡ ἱ., at Chalcis, Ael. VH 6.1 (cf. ἱπποβότης) ; esp. of the plain of Argos, from the rich pastures of Lerna, Il. 2.287, al., B. 10.80, E. Supp. 365 (lyr.).
ὁ, horse-herd, horse-keeper, S. Fr. 1057, E. Ph. 28.
ὠδῖνες pangs that gave birth to a horse and man (Pegasus and Chrysaor), Lyc. 842.
οἱ, crane-cavalry, Luc. VH 1.13.
ον, gen. ονος, judging well of horses ; hence generally, quick in judging, τινος A. Fr. 243, cf. Hsch.
οἱ, vulture-cavalry, Luc. VH 1.13.
οῦ, ὁ, = ἱππόδαμος, Poll. 1.181, Hsch.
as pr. n., Hippodamia, Il. 2.742, etc.
ἐφίππων, Hsch.

ον, (< δαμάω) tamer of horses, Hom., epith. of heroses, Il. 2.23, Od. 3.17 ; Τρῶες Il. 4.352, etc. ; Γερηνοί Hes. Fr. 15 ; ἥρωες Pi. N. 4.29 ; — fem. Ἱπποδάμεια, as pr. n., Hippodamia, Il. 2.742, etc.
ἡ, fem. Adj., Ep. epith. of κόρυς and κυνέη, bushy with horsehair, 3.369, Od. 22.111, etc.
ων, τά, horse-bands, reins, E. Hipp. 1225 ; Adj. δακτύλιοι ἱππόδεσμοι snaffle-rings, IG2². 1542.25.
ον ; v. ἱππόδεσμα.
ου, ὁ, binding horses, ῥυτήρ S. Aj. 241 (anap.) ; epith. of Heracles at Thebes and Onchestos, Paus. 9.26.1.
ον, whirled in chariots, Συρακόσιοι, B. 5.2.
ου, ὁ, Dor. ἱπποδιώκτας, = ἱππηλάτης, driver or rider of steeds, Theoc. 14.12, Hsch. ; a kind of gladiator, IGRom. 4.1455 (Smyrna).

ἡ, horse-race or chariot-race, Pi. P. 4.67, I. 3.13, X. Smp. 1.2, Pl. Ion 537a, Arist. Ath. 60.1, IG2². 784 (iii BC), SIG 730.30 (Olbia, i BC) ; ἱ. ἄγειν Ar. Pax 900 ; ποιεῖν Th. 3.104 ; ἱ. παιδική, ἣν καλοῦσι Τροίαν, = Lat. ludus Troiae, Plu. Cat. Mi. 3.
ή. όν, of horse-racing, ἀγών Sch. Il. 23.757.

ον, of the horse-race :
ἱπποδρόμιος, ὁ (sc. μήν), name of month in Boeotia, IG 7.531, al. (Tanagra), cf. Plu. Cam. 19 ; at Delphi, GDI 1987, al. ; at Naupactus, IG 9(1).359.
epith. of Poseidon (cf. ἵππιος), Pi. I. 1.54.

ὁ, chariot-road, λεῖος δ’ ἱ. ἀμφίς Il. 23.330.
race-course for chariots, Pl. Criti. 117c, D. 47.53 ; at Olympia, Paus. 6.20.15 ; at Delphi, SIG 636.24 (ii BC) ; at Andania, IG 5(1).1390.31 ; at Rome, the circus, DH. 1.79 ; ὁ μέγας ἱ., = circus maximus, Id. 5.36, Mon.Anc.Gr. 10.8 ; comic metaph, ἱ. οὗτός ἐστί σου μαγειρικῆς Posidipp. 26.23.
ὁ, light horseman, ἱ. ψιλοί Hdt. 7.158.
ἡ, acc. -ζώνην, f.l. for ὑπὸ ζώνην, Hippiatr. 26 ; the gloss in Hsch. is missing.
Adv., (< ἵππος) forth from the horse, of the heroes descending from the Trojan horse, Od. 8.515, 11.531.
ἡ, = equa, Gloss.
ου, ὁ, ass which has been suckled by a mare, such being kept for the stud, acc. to Arist. HA 577b17.
ον, swiftriding, Hsch. ; in Il. only as pr. n.
ὁ, (< θόρνυμι) covering mares, esp. of a he-ass kept for breeding mules, Hsch. as Adj., ἱ. νόμος a tune played to a mare, while she was being covered, Plu. 2.138b, 704f.
τό, sanctuary of Hippothoon, Hsch.
sacrifice horses, τῷ Ἡλίῳ Str. 11.8.6.
= ἱππιατρός, Hippiatr. 27, CIG 1953 (Maced.), POxy. 92 (iv AD).
τό, Dim. of ἱππόκαμπος, Epich. 115. a kind of ear-ring, Poll. 5.97.

ὁ, monster with horse΄s body and fish΄s tail, on which the sea-gods rode, Men. 831 ; ἑστήκει Ποσειδῶν χάλκεος, ἔχων ἱ. ἐν τῇ χειρί Str. 8.7.2, cf. Philostr. Im. 1.8.
a small fish, the sea-horse, Dsc. 2.3, Ael. NA 14.20, Gal. 12.362.
στρουθίον τι, Hsch.
ὁ, horse-beetle, Com. word in Ar. Pax 181.
ον, travelling by means of horses ; driver of horses, epith. of Patroclus, Il. 16.126, 584, 839 ; rider, AP 9.210.
α, ον, of a centaur, S.E. M. 9.125.
ὁ, horse-centaur, half-horse half-man, Pl. Phdr. 229d, X. Cyr. 4.3.17 ; also as fem., θήλειαν ἱ. ἐποίησεν Luc. Zeux. 3.
ορος, stinging horses, Tz. H. 9 No.290tit.
ου, ὁ, (< κλείω) pudenda muliebria, Ar. Fr. 703.
τό, stable, Raccolta Lumbroso 374.
groom horses, ἱ. κάνθαρον groom his beetle, Ar. Pax 74.
ὁ, (< κομέω) groom, esquire, who attended the ἱππεύς in war, Hdt. 3.85, 88, X. HG 2.4.6 ; generally, groom, Pl. Plt. 261d, PSI 4.371.13 (iii BC), Plb. 13.8.3, etc. ; ἱ. τῶν καμήλων Philostr. VA 2.1.
ον, (< κόμη) Adj., decked with horsehair, epith. of a helmet (not in Od.), κόρυς Il. 13.132, cf. S. Ant. 116 (anap.) ; πήληξ Il. 16.797 ; τρυφάλεια 13.339.
ον, coined as compd. of ἵππος and κόρυς, Porph. ad Il. 2.1 (v.l. ἱπποκόρυθες as nom. pl.).
οῦ, ὁ, marshaller, arranger of chariots, ἀνέρες ἱπποκορυσταί Il. 2.1, 24.677 ; epith. of the Paeonians, 16.287, 21.205.
τά, horse-trappings, Hsch. s.v. φάλαρα, Charis. p. 549K., Gloss.
ὁ, tender of horses, epith. of Poseidon at Sparta, Paus. 3.14.2.
α, ον, Hippocratic, διδασκαλία Gal. 6.753, cf. 15.147 ; ἀπολίνωσις Paul.Aeg. 6.78. Adv. -ως Gal. UP 8.3.
to be superior in horse, D. 19.148, Plb. 3.66.2, Onos. 31.1 ; — Pass., to be in ferior in horse, Th. 6.71.
ἡ, victory in a cavalry action, X. Cyr. 1.4.24.
ορος, ὁ, the constellation Centaurus, Teucer in Boll Sphaera 20.
ον, tremendously steep, ἱ. ῥῆμα a neck-breaking word, Ar. Ra. 929.
ἡ, = Ἵππου κρήνη, the spring of Pegasus on Helicon, v.l. in Str. 9.2.25.
ον, sounding with the tramp of horses, ὁδός Pi. P. 5.92 ; γυμνάσια E. Hipp. 229 (anap.) ; ἱ. δάπεδα γυμνάσιά τε Id. Hel. 207 (lyr.), cf. AP 12.131 (Posidipp.) ; in late Prose, Chor. Lyd. 17.
κυνος, ἡ, half-mare half-bitch, epith. of the moon-goddess, PMagPar. 1.2614.
τό, Rumex aquaticus, dock-sorrel, Dsc. 2.115, Gal. 12.56.
ῆνος, ὁ, a sort of moss used in farriery, Sch. Nic. Th. 945.
ου, ὁ, (< ὄλλυμι) destroyer of horses, Hdn. Epim. 211.
ές, having given birth to a horse, Δηώ Orac. ap. Paus. 8.42.6.
τὰς τριχίνους σειρὰς Πάρθυι οὕτω καλοῦσιν, Hsch. (-λημπρα cod., fort. -λήμπτρας).
ἔνθα τοὺς ἵππους ἀπένιζον, Hsch.
ἡ, horse΄s mane, Iamb. post Polem. p. 50 Hinck.
ον, with horsehair crest, κόρυς IG 12(2).129 (Mytilene) ; ἱ. λόγοι, by comic metaph, Ar. Ra. 818.
ον, letting horses loose, dub.l. in APl. 4.44 (fort. ἱππελάτης).
to be a-horsing, of mares, Arist. HA 572a10.

ές, abounding in, swarming with horses (cf. καρπο-, ὑλο-, φυλλο-μανής), λειμών S. Aj. 143 (anap.) ; variously expld. by Sch. as Subst., ἱππομανές, έος, τό, an Arcadian plant, thorn-apple, Datura stramonium, of which horses are madly fond, or which makes them mad, Theoc. 2.48 ; f.l. for -φαές in Thphr. HP 9.15.6. = κάππαρις, Dsc. 2.173 ; = ἀπόκυνον, Ps.-Dsc. 4.80.
small black fleshy substance on the forehead of a new-born foal, which, if procured before it was eaten off by the dam, was held to be a powerful φίλτρον, Arist. HA 577a9, 605a2, Thphr. Fr. 175, Ael. NA 3.17, 14.18.
mucous humour that runs from mares a-horsing, used for like purposes, Arist. HA 572a21, Paus. 5.27.3.
ἡ, mad love for horses, Luc. Nigr. 29.
τό, horse-fennel, Prangos ferulacea, Diocl. Fr. 155, Thphr. HP 6.1.4, Dsc. 3.71, Zopyr. ap. Orib. 14.64.1, etc. ; sts. misspelt -μάραθρον in codd.
fight on horseback, Th. 4.124, X. Cyr. 6.4.18 ; ἱ. πρὸς ὁπλίτας to fight, cavalry against infantry, Id. Ages. 2.3.
ἡ, horse-fight, action of cavalry, Th. 2.22, 4.72, Pl. La. 193b, etc.
ή, όν, of a horse-fight, νίκη St.Byz. s.v. Ἀλάβανδα.
ον (parox., Hdn. Gr. 1.230), fighting on horseback, trooper, Il. 10.431 (v.l. -δαμοι), Simon. 107.8 (= IG 7.53), Luc. Macr. 17, IG 9(1).871 (Corc., iii/ii BC).
οντος, ὁ, horse-ruler, as a pr. n., A., etc. [In Th. 488, with the 2nd syll. long, metri gr.]
ὁ, ἡ, skilled in horses or in riding, Pi. I. 7 (6).12.
ές, partly a horse, half-horse half-man, Ael. VH 9.16.
Ἱππομολγός, ff. ll. for ἱππημολγία, ἱππημολγός.
ον, horse-shaped, horse-like, Pl. Phdr. 253c.
ηκος, ὁ, horse-ant, dub. in Arist. HA 606a5. pl., ant-cavalry, Luc. VH 1.12.
ον, victorious in the chariot-race, Gloss., prob. l. in B. 13.22 ; freq. as pr. n.
τά, prob. horsehire, Hsch.
έως, ὁ, horse-keeper, Gloss.
ον, keeping horses, Poll. 1.181.
ου, ὁ, guiding or keeping horses, S. Aj. 232 (lyr., Pors. for ἱππονόμους), E. Hipp. 1399, Ar. Nu. 571 (lyr.).
Pass., have the concept or idea of a horse, opp. its real existence, Plu. 2.1120d, 1121a ; cf. ἀνθρωπόομαι.
ον, with large cheeks, Apollon.Soph. Lex. s.v. ἱππόβοτον.
ἡ, horse-fetter, Hippiatr. 106. a name given by Eudoxus to a figure-of-eight curve described by a planet, Simp. in Cael. 497.3, Procl. in Euc. pp. 127, 128F.
ῶν, αἱ, saddlebags, Sen. Ep. 87.7.
οἱ, horse-hoofed men, name of a fabulous tribe in Sarmatia, DP. 310.
ον, herding horses, of the Thracians, Il. 13.4, 14.227. (Cf. αἰπόλος, βου-κόλος.)
prob. corrupt for ἵππορ, Lacon. for ἵππος, Hsch.
κοιλάς, αὐλή, δῶμα, Hsch.
ὁ, ἡ, excessive prostitute, Ath. 13.565c, Alciphr. 1.38, al. ; cf. ἵππος VII ; also, one on horseback, Diog. ap. Eust. 1909.63.
ὁ, hippopotamus, Dsc. 2.23, Gal. 14.241, Dam. Isid. 98 ; — also ἱπποποτάμις (for -ποτάμιος), ὁ, POxy. 1220.21 (iii AD).
ον, horse-faced, epith. of the Moon-goddess, PMagPar. 1.2549 ; of a fabulous tribe, Peripl. M.Rubr. 62.

ὁ, horse, ἡ, mare, most freq. fem. in Poets ; in full θήλεες ἵπποι Il. 5.269 ; ἵπποι θήλειαι 11.680, Od. 4.635 ; ἄρσενες ἵπποι 13.81, cf. Hdt. 3.86, Pl. Hp. Ma. 288b ; pl., ἵπποι team of chariot-horses, Il. 16.370, al. ; freq. in dual, 5.237, 8.41, al. ; hence, of the chariot itself, ἀφ’ ἵπποιϊν, ἀφ’ ἵππων, from the chariot, Il. 5.13, 19, al. ; καθ’ ἵππων ἆλτο, ἐξ ἵππων βῆσε, ib. 111, 163 ; ἵππων ἐπιβησόμενος intending to mount his chariot, ib. 46 ; opp. πεζοί, πλῆτο δὲ πᾶν πεδίον πεζῶν τε καὶ ἵππων Od. 14.267, cf. 9.49 ; ἵπποι τε καὶ ἀνέρες Il. 2.554 ; λαός τε καὶ ἵπποι 18.153 ; of riders, νῶθ’ ἵππων ἐπιβάντες ἐθύνεον Hes. Sc. 286 ; freq. of race-horses, ἵ. ἀκαμαντόποδες Pi. O. 3.4 ; ἀελλόποδες Simon. 7 ; ἀθληταί Lys. 19.63 ; metaph, ἁλὸς ἵ., of ships, Od. 4.708, cf. Secund. Sent. 17. the constellation Pegasus, Eudox. ap. Hipparch. 1.2.12, Ptol. Tetr. 27, Vett.Val. 12.11. title of Hecate in the Mithraic cult, Porph. Abst. 4.16. perh. an instrument of torture, Lat. eculeus, Plu. Luc. 20 (pl.). as Collective Noun, ἵππος, ἡ, horse, cavalry, ἡ τῶν Θεσσαλῶν ἵ. Hdt. 5.64, etc. ; always in sg., even with numerals, ἵ. χιλίη a thousand horse, Id. 7.41 ; μυρίη ibid. ; μυρία, τρισμυρία, A. Pers. 302, 315 ; ἡ διακοσία ἵ. Th. 1.62 ; ἵππον ἔχω εἰς χιλίαν X. Cyr. 4.6.2.
a sea-fish, Antim. et Numen. ap. Ath. 7.304e ; but ὁ ἵ. ὁ ποτάμιος the hippopotamus, Hdt. 2.71, Arist. HA 502a9 ; ὁ ἵ. τοῦ Νείλου Ach.Tat. 4.2.
lewd woman, Ael. NA 4.11.
pudenda muliebria et virilia, Hsch.
a complaint of the eyes, such that they are always winking, Gal. 16.611, al. (also in Hp., acc. to [Gal.] 19.436).
title of ministrants (΄chuckersout΄) in certain religious ceremonies, IG2². 1368.144 (Athens, ii AD), 3.1280a.
in compds., to express anything large or coarse, as in our horse-chestnut, horse-laugh, v. ἱππόκρημνος, -λάπαθον, -μάραθον, -πορνος, -σέλινον, -τυφία, and cf. βου-.
(From ἴκϝος, v. ἴκκος ; cf. Skt. aśvas, Lat. equus ; the ἴ- (in place of e-) and the aspirate are unexplained ; the latter acc. to Gell. 2.3.2 was confined to Attic ; cf. Λεύκ-ιππος, Γλαύκ-ιππος.)
ου, ὁ, one who leads a horse by the rein, Anacr. 75.6.
τό, Alexanders, Smyrnium olus-atrum, Thphr. HP 2.2.1, Arist. Pr. 923a34, Dsc. 3.67 ; metaph, γελᾶν ἱπποσέλινα Pherecr. 131.4.
ές, with horse΄s legs, ἄνθρωπος Gal. UP 3.1.
ὁ, inspector of horses, PPetr. 3 pp. 157, 158 (iii BC).
ου, ὁ, (< σεύω) driving horses, ἄνδρες Pi. P. 2.65 ; Ἰόλαος Id. I. 5 (4).32 ; — fem. ἱπποσόα, epith. of Artemis, Id. O. 3.26 (as Subst., Pae. 9.7) ; — also ἱπποσσόος, ον, Nonn. D. 37.320.
= ἱπποσόας.
ἡ, = ἱππόστασις, Hippiatr. 29.
τό, = ἱππόστασις, Lys. Fr. 56S. ; pl., App. Pun. 95, Mith. 84.

εως, ἡ, stable, Plb. 13.8.3, Ph. 2.307 (pl.), Poll. 1.184, Anon. Oxy. 1368.46 ; metaph, Ἀελίου κνεφαία ἱππόστασις the dark stable of the Sun, i.e. the West, E. Alc. 594 (lyr.) ; but Ἕω φαεννὰς Ἡλίου θ’ ἱπποστάσεις, of the East, Id. Fr. 771.5.

ἡ, (< ἵππος) the art of driving the war-chariot ; generally, driving, horsemanship, ἱπποσύνῃ… πεποιθώς Il. 4.303, cf. 11.503 ; ἔξοχοι ἱπποσύνᾳ Simon. 108 (= IG1². 946) ; in pl., λελασμένος ἱπποσυνάων Il. 16.776, Od. 24.40 ; ἱπποσύνας ἐδίδαξαν Il. 23.307. = ἵππος II, horse, cavalry, Orac. ap. Hdt. 7.141.
η, ον, = ἱππικός, Δαρδανία E. Or. 1392 (lyr.) ; unless ἱπποσύνα is Dor. gen. from nom. ἱπποσύνης, ὁ, cf. Sch., or ἱπποσύνᾳ be read.
ἵππων τάξεις μισθοφόρων, Hsch.
ὁ, Ep. form of ἱππότης.
ὁ, horse-bull, Hld. 10.29.
ονος, ὁ, maker of the Trojan horse, Lyc. 930.
ητος, ἡ, horse-nature, the concept of horse, Antisth. et Pl. ap. Simp. in Cat. 208.30, 32, Sch. Aristid. p. 167F.

ου, ὁ, driver or rider of horses, horseman, knight, Hdt. 7.55, 9.49, 69 ; in Hom. always in Ep. nom. ἱππότα, as Γερήνιος ἱππότα Νέστωρ Il. 2.336, etc. ; ἱππότης Κολωνός S. OC 59 ; ἱππότης on horseback, Luc. Tox. 47 ; τοὶ ἱππότη, Boeot. for οἱ ἱππεῖς, IG 7.3087 (Lebad.), cf. Ascl.Tact. 10.2. Adj., ἱππόται λαοί Pi. P. 4.153 ; ἱ. λεώς the horse, A. Th. 80 (lyr.) ; λεὼν ἄνιππον ἱ. τε S. OC 899 ; ἱ. ὄχλος E. Supp. 660 ; στρατός Plu. Aem. 9. — Never used in correct Att. Prose.
ιδος, ὁ, a large kind of tiger, DC. 77.6 ; cf. ἵππος V.II.
ὁ, (< τιλάω) diarrhoea of horses, Hippiatr. 56.
ιδος, fem. of ἱππότης, Tryph. 670, Nonn. D. 1.172.
ον, horse-bearing, of Medusa, Nonn. D. 47.693.
ἡ, the art of the ἱπποτοξότης, Tz. H. 6.996, 998.
ου, ὁ, mounted bowman horse-archer, Hdt. 9.49, 4.46 ; employed as police at Athens, Th. 2.13, Lys. 15.6 ; Com., ἱέρακας ἱ. Ar. Av. 1179.
ὁ, horse-goat-stag, a fabulous monster ; used of a cup made to represent it, Philem. 87.
τό, place for horse-breeding, stud-stable, Str. 5.1.4, 16.2.10 (-τρόφιον).

aor. -τρόφησα Paus. 3.8.1 ; pf. -τρόφηκα DL. 8.51, (καθ-) Is. 5.43 ; but ἱπποτετρόφηκα Lycurg. 139 codd. : — breed or keep horses, Lycurg. l.c., Isoc. 16.33, Hyp. Lyc. 16, Satyr. 1 ; ἱπποτροφοῦσα πόλις Aen.Tact. 26.4 ; feed horses, ποᾷ χλωρᾷ Dsc. 4.15 (v.l. πόαν χλωράν).

ἡ, breeding or keeping of horses, esp. for racing, ἱ. γὰρ οὐ Ζακύνθῳ… ὀπαδεῖ Simon. 15 ; freq. in pl., ἱπποτροφίας νομίζειν Pi. I. 2.38, cf. X. Oec. 2.6, Pl. Ly. 205c, Arist. Pol. 1289b35, Anon. Oxy. 664.27 ; sg., Th. 6.12, Plu. Ages. 20. as a liturgy, ἀτελὴς ἔσται… ἱπποτροφίας SIG 1003.26 (Priene, ii BC).
ή, όν, of or for horse-keeping ; ἱπποτροφικόν, τό, allowance made to ἱπποτρόφοι, PTheb. Bank 6.8 (ii BC).

ον, (parox.) horse-feeding, abounding in horses, of Thrace, Hes. Op. 507 ; of Argos, Pi. N. 10.41 ; πόλις B. 10.114. of persons, breeding and keeping race-horses, Pi. I. 4 (3).32, etc. ; μέγας καὶ λαμπρὸς ἱ. D. 18.320, cf. Plu. Them. 5, Paus. 6.2.1. generally, horsebreeder, POxy. 2110.6 (iv AD), Hippiatr. 34.
ἡ, (< τῦφος) horse-pride, i.e. excessive pride or conceit, Luc. Hist. Conscr. 45, Pl. ap. DL. 3.39.
τό, = ἵππουρος, horse-tail, Arat. 438.
έως, ὁ, = ἵππουρος, Hices. ap. Ath. 7.304c.

ιδος, ἡ, (< οὐρά) as fem. Adj., horse-tailed, decked with a horse-tail, freq. in Hom. (esp. Il.), in nom. and acc. ἵππουρις, ιν, κόρυς Il. 6.495 ; τρυφάλεια 19.382 ; κυνέη Od. 22.124. as Subst., horse-tail, Ael. NA 16.21 ; Satyr΄s tail, Phryn. PS p. 77B. a water-plant, horse-tail, Equisetum silvaticum, Dsc. 4.46, Ps.-Democr. in Gp. 2.6.27 ; also, = Equisetum maximum, Dsc. 4.47.
a complaint in the groin, caused by constant riding, dub. in Hp. Epid. 7.122.

ον, (< οὐρά) horse-tailed ; as Subst., a sea-fish, Coryphaena hippurus, Epich. 51, Arist. HA 543a23, Numen. ap. Ath. 7.304d, Oppian. H. 1.184. a kind of insect, Ael. NA 15.1. = ἵππουρις ΙΙ. 2, Hippiatr. 27.
οἱ, horse-eaters, name of a Scythian tribe, Ptol. Geog. 5.9.

έος, τό, a kind of spurge, Euphorbia spinosa, used for carding cloth, Asclep. ap. Gal. Nat. Fac. 1.13, Dsc. 4.159 (also ἱππόφαος ibid., ἱπποφανής Ps.-Dsc. ibid.). = ἱππόφαιστον, Ps.-Dsc. 4.160 ; = ἱππόφεως, Gal. 19.106 ; as a drug, Thphr. HP 9.15.6.
τό, a plant, Centaurea spinosa, Dsc. 4.160, Plin. HN 27.92, Ruf. ap. Orib. 7.26.37.
εω, ὁ, spurge, Euphorbia acanthothamnos, gen. -φεω (v.l. -φαέως, φέως) Hp. Int. 13, 25, 26 ; nom. -φεως Thphr. HP 6.5.2. = ἐπίθυμον, Plin. HN 26.55, Gloss.
ὁ, giant φλόμος, i.e. belladonna, Atropa belladonna, Plin. HN 25.148.
άδος, ἡ, horse-fear, a fabulous plant, Ps.-Democr. ap. Plin. HN 24.161.
άδος, fem. of ἱπποφορβεύς.
έως, ὁ, = ἱπποφορβός, Poll. 7.185 ; — fem. ἱπποφορβάς, άδος, Sch. Luc. Ind. 5.
= keep horses, Choerob. in Theod. 2lxxxv.
ἡ, horse-keeping, Pl. Plt. 299d.
τό, herd of horses, Hdt. 4.110, X. HG 4.6.6, Arist. HA 576a20. = ἱπποτροφεῖον, E. El. 623, Arist. HA 576a25, Ph. 2.307.
όν, (< φέρβω) horse-keeper, Pl. Plt. 261d, Arist. HA 577a15, Jul. Or. 7.227c ; as Adj., ἱ. γῆ DH. 1.37. αὐλὸς ἱ. a flute used by ἱπποφορβοί, made of laurel bark, Poll. 4.74.
ου, ὁ, = ἱππιοχάρμης, Pi. O. 1.23, Pae. 2.104.
ονος, dub.sens., Tab. Defix. Aud. 38.29 (Alexandria, iii AD).
ες, horse-like, X. Eq. 1.11 (Comp.), Poll. 1.192 ; κεφαλή Hippiatr. 14.
ες, riding in a swift chariot, ἀέλιος B. 10.101.
(< ὠνέομαι) buy horses, X. Eq.Mag. 1.14, Eq. 11.13.

Ion. -ίη, ἡ, buying of horses, X. Eq.Mag. 1.12 (with v.l. ἱππωνεία, which is found in codd. of Eq. 1.1, 3.1), Poll. 1.182.
tax on sale of horses, SIG 4 (Cyzicus, vi BC).

ῶνος, ὁ, place for horses ; stable, IG1². 336 (pl.), X. Eq. 4.2, Moschio ap. Ath. 5.207f, PCair. Zen. 193.5 (iii BC).
posting-house, station, X. Cyr. 8.6.17, Supp.Epigr. 2.481 (Scythia, iii AD).
= πέτομαι, Mosch. 3.43, Babr. 65.4, Jul. Or. 2.72a, etc. ; censured by Luc. Sol. 7, Lex. 25.

*ἴπτομαι, fut. ἴψομαι ; aor.1 ἰψάμην : — press hard, oppress, μέγα δ’ ἴψαο λαὸν Ἀχαιῶν Il. 1.454, 16.237 ; τάχα δ’ ἴψεται υἷας Ἀχαιῶν 2.193 ; generally, hurt, harm, σὺ τόνδε μηρὸν ἴψω ; Theoc. Adon. 19, cf. Str. 8.6.7 ; — Act., ἴπτω, = βλάπτω, only in EM 481.3 ; ἶψαι, ἴψας, Hsch. (Perh. related to ἰάπτω 2 or to ἶπος.)
ἡ, = σιπύα, Hsch. (prob. ἱπύα).
ἀρχή τις, Hsch. (prob. = ἱππαρμοστής).
εως, ἡ, (< ἰπόω) pressing hard, squeezing, esp. in reducing dislocations, Hp. Art. 47, Heliod. ap. Orib. 49.27.5 and 32.7.

τό, olive- or wine-press, ἰ. ληνοῦ, Gloss. ; ὅλμοι καὶ ἰ. PRev. Laws 49.13, cf. 51.2 (iii BC). in surgery, bougie, Heliod. ap. Orib. 50.9.7, Antyll. ap. eund. 44.23.61, Meges ap. eund. 44.24.9. name of a plaster, Heracl. Tarent. ap. Gal. 13.725, Orib. Fr. 52.
ίδος, ἡ, for pressing in dislocated joints, σπάθη Heliod. ap. Orib. 49.32.4 and 17.9.
ῶν, αἱ, v.l. for εἶραι, Il. 18.531 ; v. εἴρη.
v. εἰρήνη.
τό, = ἠράνθεμον, Hippiatr. 44.
Ion. for ἱεράομαι.
v. ἱέρεια.
v. ἱέρεια.
v. ἱέρεια.
Ion. for ἱέρεια.
v.l. for εἴρερος.
Ion. and Ep. for ἱερεύς.
Ion. and Ep. for ἱερεύω.
v. ἱέρεια.
Ion. and Ep. for ἱερεῖον.
ένος, ὁ, Ion. for εἰρήν, prob. in Hdt. 9.85.
ηκος, ὁ, Ion. and Ep. for ἱέραξ.
ἡ, (< ἱεράομαι) priestess, Hsch.
Lesb. for ἱερατεύω.
to be iridescent, PHolm. 7.6.
ἵππος οἰνωπὸς χρώματι, Hsch.
α, ον, = ἴρινος, Nic. Al. 203, 241.
ον, mixed with iris-oil, Philox. 2.40.
η, ον, made from the iris, μύρον Pl.Com. 69.7, Cephisod. 3.2, Alex. 62.8, Thphr. HP 9.9.2, Plb. 30.26.2.
ές, rainbow-like, Luc. Hist. Conscr. 19, Olymp. in Mete. 230.21, al.

ἡ, gen. ἴριδος Thphr. CP 6.11.13, also εως Androm. ap. Gal. 14.43, POxy. 1088.34 (i AD), Gp. 6.8.1 ; acc. ἶριν Michel l.c., Plu. 2.664e, ἴριδα Nic. Al. 406 ; Ep. dat. pl. ἴρισσιν (v. infr.) : — rainbow, δράκοντες…, ἴρισσιν ἐοικότες, ἅς τε Κρονίων ἐν νέφεϊ στήριξε, τέρας μερόπων ἀνθρώπων Il. 11.27, cf. Arist. Mete. 375a1, Epicur. Ep. 2 p. 51U. any bright-coloured circle surrounding another body, as the lunar rainbow, Arist. Mete. 375a18 ; halo of candle, Thphr. Sign. 13 ; round the eyes of a peacock΄s tail, Luc. Dom. 11 ; the iris of the eye, Ruf. Onom. 24, [Gal.] 14.702 ; also, section through the ciliary region, Gal. UP 10.2.
iridescent garment, Michel l.c. various species of the botanical genus iris, e.g.
the purple Iris, I. germanica or pallida, εὐάνθεμον ἶριν AP 4.1.9 (Mel.) ; τὸ ἄνθος πολλὰς ἔχει ἐν αὑτῷ ποικιλίας Arist. Col. 796b26, cf. Plin. HN 21.40 ; also, the white variety of it, I. florentina, from the rhizome of which the orris-root of commerce is made, Thphr. HP 1.7.2, CP 6.11.13, etc. ; ἶρις Ἰλλυρική Dsc. 1.1, cf. Plin. HN 13.14 ; in this sense some wrote it oxyt. ἰρίς, ίδος, Eust. 391.33, Sch. Nic. l.c. a precious stone, Plin. HN 37.136.

ιδος, ἡ, acc. Ἶριν, voc. Ἶρι ; — Iris, the messenger of the gods among themselves, Il. 8.398 (never in Od.), Hes. Th. 780, etc. (Perh. fr. Ϝῖρις, cf. ὠκέα Ἶρις Il. 2.786, al., Hes. l.c. ; ὦκα δὲ Ἶρις Il. 23.198 (Pap.) ; possibly also fr. *Ἐϝῖρις ; Εἶρις is the name of a ship, IG2². 1611c137 (iv BC), but ἶρις is written in Michel 832 (Samos, iv BC) ; allegorized as προφορικὸς λόγος and derived from εἴρω by Stoic. 2.43).
ες, like the rainbow, Arist. Mete. 374a28.
ὁ, perh. sack-bearer, Schwyzer 230 (vi BC).
ὁ, poet. for ἱεροδρόμος.
Ion. for ἱερολογέω.
Ion. for ἱερολογία.
τό, Ion. for ἱερόν.
ὁ, ἡ, priest or priestess, IG 3.736, 5(2).461 (Megalop.).
v. ἱερουργία.
Aeol. for ἱερός.
Ion. and Ep. for ἱερός, but also in Att. Poets, v. ἱερός sub fin.

ὁ, Irus, a name given by the suitors to the Ithacan beggar Arnaeus because he carried messages (cf. Ἶρις), Od. 18.5 sq. ; hence, later as Appellat., an Irus, i.e. a beggar, Lib. Or. 18.140 ; pl., Ἶροι Luc. Nav. 24.
ὁ, Ion. for ἱεροφάντης.
poet. for ἱεροφύλαξ.
ὁ, ἡ, gen. ονος, of sacred earth, βῶλος IG 14.1389i i 27.
Ion. and Ep. contr. for ἱερο-.
ῶνος, ὁ, perh. = region, dub. word in Inscr.Cypr. 135.8, 31 H. (where toironi may be τοῖ οἰρῶνι ; v. οἰρών).
Ion. for ἱερωστί, in sacred fashion, Anacr. 149.
ἡ, Ion. for ἱερωσύνη, priesthood, v.l. in Hdt. 4.161.

ἡ, gen. ἰνός, acc. ἶνα, nom. pl. ἶνες, dat. ἴνεσι Il. 23.191, also ἰσίν Sor. (v. infr.), Suid. s.v. ἶνες, cj. Nauck for εἰσίν in A. Fr. 229 : — sinew, tendon, sg. once in Hom., ὡς δ’ ὅτ’ ἂν… ἀνὴρ… ἶνα τάμῃ διὰ πᾶσαν Il. 17.522 ; usu. in pl., sinews, οὐ γὰρ ἔτι σάρκας τε καὶ ὀστέα ἲνες ἔχουσιν Od. 11.219, cf. Il. 23.191 ; ἶνες ἄρθρων Ar. Pax 86, cf. Archil. 138 ; ἶνες αὐτὸ μόνον καὶ λεπτὴ δορά, of a person wasted by disease, Ph. 2.432 ; δοράς, σάρκας, ἶνας ib. 527 ; metaph, Τρωίας ἶνας ἐκταμὼν δορί Pi. I. 8 (7).57. later, the fibrous vessels in the muscles, Pl. Ti. 84a, Arist. HA 515b27, al. ; in blood, fibrine, Id. PA 650b14, cf. Pl. Ti. 82c, Meno Iatr. 17.34 ; metaph, of metals, Plu. 2.434b.
rib in the leaves of plants, Thphr. HP 3.12.7 (sg.).
strip of papyrus, ταῖς τῶν χαρτῶν ἰσίν Sor. 1.13 ; sg., Gal. 10.1000. λεπτὴ ἴς a small fibre of papyrus, Id. 17(1).795.

ἡ, three times in acc. sg. ἶνα (elided ἶν΄) Il. 5.245, 7.269, Od. 9.538, freq. in instr. ἶφι, elsewh. only nom. sg. : — strength, force, of persons, ἀλλ’ ἄρα καὶ ἲς ἐσθλή Il. 12.320 ; ἐπέρεισε δὲ ἶν’ ἀπέλεθρον 7.269 ; ἤ μοι ἔτ’ ἐστὶν ἴς, οἵη πάρος. Od. 21.283, cf. 11.393, 18.3 ; freq. in periphr., ἱερὴ ἲς Τηλεμάχοιο the strong Telemachus, 2.409 ; κρατερὴ ἲς Ὀδυσῆος Il. 23.720 ; ἲς Ἡρακλῆος Hes. Th. 951 ; and in twofold periphr., ἲς βίης Ἡρακληείης ib. 332 ; also of things, ἲς ἀνέμου or ἀνέμοιο, Il. 15.383, 17.739, Od. 9.71 ; ἲς ποταμοῖο Il. 21.356 ; κράται’ ἴς was read by Ptol.Ascal. in Od. 11.597 ; v. κρατύς. (ϝι-, cf. γίς· ἰσχύς, Hsch., pr. n. Ϝιφιάδας IG 7.3172.70, Lat. vis, vim ; prob. cogn. with ἵεμαι but not with ἴς¹.)
ον, like an angel, Ev. Luc. 20.36, Hierocl. in CA 4 p. 425M.
ον, like a brother, of Pylades, E. Or. 1015 (anap.) ; εὔνοια IPE 1². 359.

— Pass., fut. ἰσασθήσομαι Arist. EE 1243b31 ; aor.1 ἰσάσθην Id. EN 1133a14 ; pf. ἴσασμαι ib. b5 ; (< ἴσος) : — make equal, balance, of a person holding scales, σταθμὸν… καὶ εἴριον… ἀνέλκει ἰσάζουσ’ Il. 12.435 ; ἰ. τὰς κτήσεις to equalize them, Arist. Pol. 1265a38 ; ἰ. τὸ ἄνισον Id. EN 1132a7 ; τὴν φιλίαν ib. 1163b33 ; — Med., make oneself equal to another, οὕνεκ’ ἄρα Λητοῖ ἰσάσκετο (sc. Νιόβη) Il. 24.607 ; — Pass., to be made or to be equal, θεοῖς Pl. Ti. 41c ; abs., Arist. EN 1133a14, al. ; μήκει ποδὸς ἴχνος ἰσάζεται Nic. Th. 286 ; δίστιχα ψήφοισιν ἰσάζεται AP 9.356 (Leon.).
intr. in Act., to be equal, Pl. Lg. 773a, Arist. EN 1154b24 ; ἀλλήλοις Id. Pol. 1304a39.
to be even, normal, Hp. Morb. 4.49. [ι in Hom. ; ι in Nic. Th. 286, 886.]
ον, equal to the Immortals, καρπός Arist. Fr. 675.7 as quoted by Did. in D. (6.37).
poet. for ἰσάζομαι, resemble, Nic. Al. 399, Fr. 74.56 ; to be made equal, Arat. 235, 513 ; — Act., ἰσαίω is implied in ἰσήι (Boeot. for ἰσαίει)· ἰσοῖ, ἰσάζει, Hsch.
α, ον, late poet. form of ἴσος, Nic. Th. 360 ; — ἡ ἰσαία (sc. μοῖρα), equality, ἐπ’ ἰσαίῃ Call. Jov. 63, cf. Philostr.Jun. Im. 3 ; τὰ ἰσαῖα (ἰσεα lapis) an equal share, SIG 57.10 (Milet., v BC).
ἰσαίτατος, v. ἴσος.

Adv. from ἴσος, the same number of times, as many times, Str. 3.5.8 ; ἰ. πολλαπλάσιος c. gen., the same multiple of…, Euc. 7 Def. 21, al. ; ἰ. πολλαπλάσια equimultiples, Id. 5 Def. 5, al. ; ἰ. ἴσος, of a number, equal multiplied by equal, i.e. square, Pl. R. 546c, Tht. 147e, 148a, Euc. 7 Def. 19, Ph. 1.11, etc. ; ἰ. ἴσος ἰ. equal multiplied by equal multiplied by equal, i.e. cube number, Euc. 7 Def. 20, etc.
ον, ranking with the Actian games, CIG 4472.11 (Laodicea ad Mare).
v. sub ἰξαλῆ.
ου, Dor. for ἰσημέριος, lasting an equal time, φύλλοις αἰγείρου S. Fr. 593.2.

v. *εἴδω 2, and add : ἴσαμι Theoc. 5.119 ; ἴσαις (2 sg.) Id. 14.34 ; ἴσατι Id. 15.146 ; ἴσατε Periand. ap. DL. 1.99 ; ἴσαντι Theoc. 15.64 ; inf. γισάμεναι (i.e. ϝισ-)· εἰδέναι, Hsch. ; Arc. ἰσάμεν (ισμεν lapis), IG 5(2).357.12 ; 3 pl. subj. ἴσαντι Schwyzer 190 (Cretan).
ον, equal in the race ; neut. pl. as Adv., ἰσάμιλλα δραμεῖν τινι AP 9.311 (Phil.).
δύσμορος, Hsch. (leg. κάμμορος).

they went, 3 pl. impf. Ep. of εἶμι (ibo), Hom.
they knew, 3 pl. plpf. Ep. of οἶδα, Il. 18.405, Od. 4.772.
ἰσάνιον, ῥητίνην, Hsch.
ον, taking the same time to rise, ζῴδια Vett.Val. 142.27 ; — also ἰσανάφορος, ον, ibid., cf. Paul.Al. E. 4, S. 2.
= ἰσανάτολος.
ον, (< ἀνήρ) like a man, Hsch.
ον, swift as the wind, E. IA 206 (lyr.).
ον, of equal worth, Porph. Abst. 2.55 ; τῷ Διΐ Procl. in Cra. p. 50 P. ; τοῖς θεοῖς Iamb. Myst. 3.21 ; adequate, πρός τι Dam. Pr. 43, cf. 28. Adv. -ίως Iamb. Myst. 9.7.
ον, worth its weight in silver, πορφυρᾶς ἰ. κηκῖδα A. Ag. 959, cf. Achae. 5, Ephipp. 21.4.
to be equal in number, τινι Tz. H. 1.939.
ον, = ἰσάριθμος, c. gen., Μουσῶν IG 14.1747.

ον, equal in number with, ψυχαὶ ἰ, τοῖς ἄστροις Pl. Ti. 41d, cf. Lg. 845a, Arist. EN 1156a7, al., Call. Del. 175, Puchstein Epigr.Gr. p. 9 ; εἰσαρίθμοις ἔπεσι, = ἰσοψήφοις, IG 5(1).257 (Laconia) ; poet. ἰσήριθμος, AP 6.84 (Paul. Sil.), 328 (Leon.), Lyc. 1258. Adv. ἰσάριθμως Gal. 19.469, Them. Or. 33.367b.
Gramm., of the same grammatical number, ADysc. Synt. 170.13.
Adv. -μως ib. 143.9.
ον, equally ancient, Choerob. in Theod. 2.55.
οντος, ὁ, equitable ruler, POxy. 41.12, 28 (iii/iv AD).
Ep. 3 sg. impf. Med. of ἰσάζω, Il. 24.607.
ὁ, equalization, Epicur. Nat. 15.21 (pl.).
ον, like a star, bright as a star, LXX 4 Ma. 17.5.
ή, όν, equalizing, handicapped, στάθμη, in a race, Eust. 1023.5.

ιδος, Hp. Ulc. 11, Michel 832 (Samos, iv BC) (but -ιος Hp. Aff. 38, -εως POxy. 101.12) ; ἡ ; — a plant producing a dark blue dye, woad, Lat. Isatis tinctoria, Hp. ll.cc., Thphr. Sens. 77, Dsc. 2.184, Plin. HN 20.59.
ες, like woad, Hp. Epid. 4.45, 2.3.1 ; χολή Aret. CD 1.15.
ες, (< αὐδή) of the same name, Theoc. Syrinx 9.
Adv., (< ἴσος) in the same number of ways, Arist. Metaph. 1013a16, al. ; παρακολουθεῖν ἰ. τινί ib. 1054a14 ; τἀγαθὸν ἰ. λέγεται τῷ ὄντι in as many ways as, Id. EN 1096a23.
v. ὕσγινον.
v. ὕσγινον.
τά, v. Ἰσιεῖα.
τό, v. Ἰσιεῖον.
to be of an intermediate age, ἰσεννύουσαι Hp. Mul. 2.111 (so Gal. 19.106 ; ἴσαι νῦν ἐουσαι Hp. codd. ; ἴσενοι ἐοῦσαι cj. Schneider (cf. ἔνος)).
ου, ὁ, (ἥβη) = ἰσῆλιξ, Tim. Pers. 226.
speak as an equal, v.l. in LXX Si. 13.11 ; — Act. ἰσηγορέω, Sch. D Il. 1.187, Hsch., Phot.

Ion. -ίη, ἡ, equal right of speech, and generally, political equality, Hdt. 5.78, Eup. 291, X. Cyr. 1.3.10, Zeno Stoic. 1.54, Phld. Hom. p. 20O., etc. ; ἰ. καὶ ἐλευθερία D. 21.124 ; ἰ. καὶ παρρησία Jul. Or. 1.17b.
ον, enjoying equal right of speech, freedom of speech, Poll. 6.174.
η, ον, equal in magnitude, τάφρος Ph.Mech. Bel. 91.21 ; equal in age, Procl. in Prm. p. 944S., al., Dam. Pr. 316.
ικος, ὁ, ἡ, of the same age with, τινι X. Smp. 8.1, Com.Adesp. 874 ; c. gen., ἰ. χρόνος κόσμου Ph. 1.6 ; abs., Id. 2.303.
ἡ, equinox, ἰ. ἐαρινή, μετοπωρινή, ὀπωρινή, Arist. Mete. 364b1, 2, 371b30 ; φθινοπωρινή Id. HA 570b14, etc. ; in pl., Hp. Aër. 11, Pl. Ax. 370c, Porph. Antr. 24.
